summary: 军报连发三文 李干杰称杜绝先斩后奏 暗指张又侠案？(图) 習近平 | 民主集中制 | 一把手 | 劉振立 | 兩個維護 | 五中全會 | 动向 || 看中国网 2024年4月22日，时任中共中央军委副主席张又侠上将在青岛举行的西太平洋海军研讨会开幕前抵达现场，向众人挥手致意。（图片来源：Kevin Frayer/Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。 【看中国2026年11月12日讯】（看中国记者李德言综合报导）五中全会过后，中共军报连
content:
军报连发三文 李干杰称杜绝先斩后奏 暗指张又侠案？(图) 習近平 | 民主集中制 | 一把手 | 劉振立 | 兩個維護 | 五中全會 | 动向 || 看中国网
2024年4月22日，时任中共中央军委副主席张又侠上将在青岛举行的西太平洋海军研讨会开幕前抵达现场，向众人挥手致意。（图片来源：Kevin Frayer/Getty Images） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
【看中国2026年11月12日讯】（看中国记者李德言综合报导）五中全会过后，中共军报连发三文，强调对军权的掌控以及“政治忠诚”、绝不能有“怀二心之人”，让人联想到习近平是否仍处于军权不稳的状态。而李干杰日前的一篇文章，虽然也提到“两个维护”，但却多次强调“民主集中制”，以及对“一把手”的限制，甚至直言“杜绝先斩后奏”等敏感话语，不由得让人联想到习近平对张又侠案的处理方式。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
2026年11月1日，中共党媒新华社发布《中共中央关于持之以恒推进全面从严治党若干重大问题的决定》。该文件在10月29日闭幕的中共五中全会上通过。
“决定”称，要落实加强对“一把手”和领导班子监督的制度规定，规范“一把手”职责权限......党委（党组）书记必须发扬民主......正确对待少数人意见，不得搞“一言堂”“家长制”......“不得层层要求维护‘一把手’个人权威”。
“决定”中反复提到的“一把手”，让人不由得想到曾被称为“定于一尊”的中共党魁习近平。
五中全会结束后，中共军报持续在头版刊登系列评论员文章。
2026年11月5日，军报在头版刊发评论员文章《当前和今后一个时期全党的重大政治任务——六谈认真学习贯彻党的二十届五中全会精神》，其中提到：“抓好常态化政治整训，紧扣备战打仗根本职能”，“下力解决坚持党对军队绝对领导、抓备战打仗能力、落实管党治党政治责任等方面的突出问题，以更高标准、更实举措抓好全面从严治党、全面从严治军各项工作。”
11月4日，军报发表的“五谈”文章《坚定不移一体推进不敢腐不能腐不想腐》强调，中共军队是拿枪杆子的，军中绝不能有对党怀有二心之人，绝不能有腐败分子藏身之地。还说要“坚定不移将反腐败斗争进行到底。”
11月3日，军报发表的“四谈”文章《贯彻落实持之以恒推进全面从严治党系统部署》声称，要持续推进全面从严治军，“毫不动摇坚持和加强党对军队的绝对领导，扭住听党指挥、政治忠诚这个根本问题，”
时评人语茗表示，按中共“缺什么、喊什么”的习性来看，军报接连发文要求“坚持党对军队绝对领导”、“军中绝不能有对党怀有二心之人”、“坚持和加强党对军队的绝对领导”，似乎透露出习近平并没有完全掌握军队主导权，而文章也提到“政治忠诚”，让人联想到习近平此前多次提及的“两面人”。
2026年1月24日，中共国防部宣布，中央军委副主席张又侠、中央军委联合参谋部参谋长刘振立被调查。1月25日，中共军报火速发表社论，极其严厉地批张、刘“严重践踏破坏军委主席负责制”等。
2026年9月21日，中共官方通报张、刘“与党离心离德、逾越红线底线、搞团团伙伙”；利用职务便利为他人职务晋升等提供帮助，收受巨额钱款；违规收受礼品礼金；“不履行全面从严治党政治责任”。强调他们存在贪腐问题。
同年9月23日，中共军报发文强调，查处张、刘“消除了重大政治隐患”。
同年10月29日傍晚，中共党媒新华社发布五中全会的会议公报，显示会议审议通过了中共中央军事委员会关于张又侠、刘振立等人开除党籍处分。
中共对张又侠、刘振立的通报主要强调两人涉及贪腐，这也和军报强调的“坚定不移将反腐败斗争进行到底”有呼应。
2026年11月6日，中共政治局委员、中央外办主任、中共外交部长王毅在中共党媒《人民日报》发表题为《中央和国家机关要走好第一方阵》的署名文章，其中强调要维护中共中央“定于一尊、一锤定音”的权威，始终“忠诚核心、拥戴核心、维护核心、捍卫核心”。这些说法很直白地在维护习近平的权威，也与“决定”提到的不得搞“一言堂”“家长制”......“不得层层要求维护‘一把手’个人权威”相对立。
2026年11月11日，《人民日报》在要闻版刊发了中共中央政治局委员、中央统战部部长李干杰的署名文章《严格贯彻执行民主集中制》，其中反复提到“民主集中制”：“着眼于党要管党、全面从严治党，就严格贯彻执行民主集中制作出重要部署”，“贯彻执行民主集中制是全面从严治党的内在要求。”“以实际行动践行‘两个维护’。要完善党中央重大决策部署落实机制，”
文章强调，“工作中的重大决策、重大事项、重要情况及时向党中央请示报告，确保全局性重大方针政策由党中央决策、重大原则和重大事项由党中央决定、重要情况报党中央知晓，坚决杜绝先斩后奏、边斩边奏、斩而不奏。”而这个“先斩后奏、边斩边奏、斩而不奏”也引发联想，未知是否暗指习近平对张又侠、刘振立先抓后报的事件。
文章也对“个人说了算”表示反对态度，称要“发扬党内民主、善于正确集中，是贯彻执行民主集中制的必然要求。要尊重党员主体地位、保障党员民主权利，”“坚决避免个人说了算、决策走过场。”“保护那些敢于讲真话、讲实话、讲心里话”的官员，这不由得让人想到在习近平面前敢于直言、与习意见不一致的张又侠。
文章还多次提及要限制“一把手”，对个人独断表示反对，“凡是重大事项、重大问题严格遵循集体领导、民主集中、个别酝酿、会议决定的原则进行集体研究决策，防止把个人凌驾于组织之上；”“清晰划定‘一把手’职责权限边界，强化对权力运行的全程监督，把权力关进位度笼子，”“要执行‘一把手’末位表态制，重大决策、重要人事任免、重大项目安排、大额资金使用等，必须经过集体讨论决定，‘一把手’不得先定调子、不得把个人意见强加给班子，”
对此，时评人婉静指出，文章虽然总共十次提及习近平，两次提到维护习近平权威的“两个维护”，并称所谓深刻领悟“两个确立”的意义、要求“坚决做到‘两个维护’”，但文章称要限制“一把手”，防止“个人凌驾于组织之上”，以及“民主集中制”，还有那句似乎意有所指的“先斩后奏”，都让人感到这些冠冕话语背后的寒光阵阵，这或许也折射出中共高层从五中全会以后持续至今的博弈，以及这种内斗的外在表现。

黄仁勋惨陷美女特务局 中共情报活动无孔不入 黄乐 | 芯片 | 时评 |颜纯钩| 看中国网
【看中国2026年11月12日讯】近日最大新闻，是辉达老板黄仁勋与中共女特务发生婚外恋情。被美国媒体揭露后，辉达对外公告展开公司内部调查，美国众议院将秘密传唤黄仁勋作供。黄仁勋也发表公开声明，承认自己对不起太太和家人，也对不起公司同仁，表示愿意配合调查。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
随着辉达惊天的企业成就，黄仁勋成为全世界华人中最有世界影响力的人，他不但富可敌国，而且成为全世界高科技企业追逐的合作目标，更参与国际政治的运作。按理，当下正是他事业最高峰，只要他保持状态，他一定会名留青史。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
一个人成就了非凡事业，他的工作与生活都是大众好奇心所在，黄仁勋与那个名叫黄乐的中国女间谍，在公共场合举止亲密，不避人嫌，导致美国情报机构的关注，他的地下恋情便一定会曝光，因此有今日之果，与他的高调很有关系。
一个人聪明绝顶，但在个人生活上如此不检点，只能说他太大意，也可能他长久以来受媒体热捧，飘飘然忘乎所以，反倒让自己陷入一个难以自拔的陷阱。一方面个人声誉受损，另方面公司商誉也遭遇无妄之灾，他自己的人设崩塌，以后再出来面对公众，便要低调做人，再回台湾，也没有那么潇洒风流了。
至于那个女间谍黄乐，原来竟是香港浸会大学传理系硕士生，据说在大陆电视台和金融机构都工作过，2023年才在新加坡成立一间高科技公司，除了在马来西亚投资AI资料中心，将算力出售给大陆阿里巴巴等公司之外，还进口辉达高阶芯片，涉款高达48亿美元。
这些芯片涉嫌违反美国禁令，购入后走私回大陆，显然，这不是黄乐的个人生意，是中共国家行为。据报道她丈夫已因金融作弊被判无期徒刑，而她参与前公司管理，又能全身而退，这本身就不正常。公司事发后，她还能得到阿里巴巴背书，继续行走高科技江湖，以至最终成为黄仁勋的情妇，其中必有国家之手在背后发功。
中共美女特务在美国和其他西方国家活动，不时都有同类新闻被揭发出来，这是中共灰色地带作战的传统手法。这些美女特务专门结交西方重要部门和领域的上层男人，从中套取民主国家的政治经济军事情报，服务中共的利益。
台湾媒体播出黄仁勋与黄乐在各种社交饭局前后一些互动片断，可见两人关系之亲密，已经到了半公开的程度。他是公众人物，一言一行都在公众眼里，奇怪的是，似乎他不介意引起异议，也不担心家人的反应，也不理会对公司商誉的影响，他是太天真，还是太自以为是？
一个人在巨大成功面前，有时会失去自省的能力，也会因为太狂妄而我行我素，但最终，“出来行迟早要还”，他今日落入自己挖的坑里，只能说咎由自取。
川普(特朗普)对黄仁勋的“中招”似乎颇理解，他说黄仁勋是好人，要看看调查结果如何，给他一个机会。川普在个人生活方面从不检点，身上背着几单强奸罪名，所以黄仁勋的婚外情，在川普眼里简直不是什么事。黄仁勋在美国政商两界吃得开，川普也要给几分脸色，所以言下留情，似乎也不令人意外。
黄仁勋中了美女特务圈套，他会不会把辉达的高科技机密泄露给中共？我反倒认为不会。因为辉达的科技机密，是黄仁勋的家底，他若把机密泄露给中共，岂不是倒自己米？中共得到辉达科技机密后，在高科技上反过来碾压辉达，黄仁勋有什么好处？
再说，现代高科技是一个庞大体系，不是三言两语可以说清楚，对黄乐那个高科技盲，更是一头雾水，跟她说她也不懂，因此黄仁勋会泄露的，可能只是美国对华禁运的一些内幕而已，那些内幕其实中共都知道七七八八，没有太大机密价值。
黄乐与黄仁勋勾搭，长远目的可能是保证购买辉达芯片这条内线，有了芯片长期供应，可以扩张算力生意，也可以将芯片走私回大陆从中谋利。她志在取得黄仁勋信任，一方面从中赚钱，另一方面完成中共交给她的偷运芯片任务。天下没有比黄仁勋亲自过问更可靠的机会了，黄乐只要做到这一点，就足以让国安当局满意了。
黄仁勋多次公开批评美国政府的芯片禁运政策，说那反而会促使中共投入更多资源去开发先进芯片，而美中之间的科技差距已经相当有限。这种说法当然没有逻辑，你不卖给中共芯片，中共被迫要自行研发，但你卖给他芯片，难道他就不研发了吗？他还指望着弯道超车美国呢？黄仁勋只不过痛惜少赚一大笔进口芯片给大陆的收入而已。
中共操作美女特务经验老到，防不胜防。早在国共内战时期，中共就往国民党军政高层派遣特务，美女特务更是“好使好用”的工具。国共内战时期，曾有一个美女特务沈安娜，潜伏到国民党中央党部任机要速记员，现场笔录蒋介石召开军政会议时口述的内战调兵指令和军事部署，情报透过地下管道直达毛泽东周恩来。蒋介石身边都有特务，其他的更可想而知了。
中共物色美女特务也不是随便的，要考察家庭背景文化程度个人性情等方面，容貌娇好当然也是首选条件。这些美女特务除了接受职业训练之外，最要紧是有放下自尊牺牲色相的意愿，一般行为端正的女孩，是不会随便将个人身体当作党的工具来用的，但有些女孩会接受，甚至乐意接受，因为有现实利益引诱，又有为国家作贡献的正当理由。
笔者在内地时曾听说，一个女孩中学刚毕业，就有公安部门找上门，希望派她到香港，没有具体任务，只管生活工作，以后有需要用到她时，组织会派人与她联络，到时才知道要做什么。这个女孩有直系亲属在台湾国军任高层，也有亲戚在香港，她外貌也很出众，又能歌善舞，符合担任美女特务的条件，但最终她父母没有答应，此事便作罢。
从这个简单例子，便可知中共在香港和海外安插了多少国安特务。他们平日就像普通华人一样生活工作，组织家庭，直到有一天，有人主动联络她，她的特务身份就复活。黄乐如果是国安特务，很大可能在学生年代就已被吸纳，直至她有机会接触到黄仁勋，于是正堪大用。
对寻常百姓来说，身边有无中共特务无关紧要，但对像黄仁勋这样的业界翘楚，他们身上集中了政经光环，又有各种利益交集，又接触国家和行业机密，他们便要明白，自己永远是中共机密行动的目标。他们对身边出入的人，都要引起高度警惕——常在水边走，哪能不湿鞋？否则，很容易就陷入中共谋划的阴谋之中，最终吃亏的还是自己。

拆局黄乐芯片交易：钱哪里来 货交给谁(图) 中国 | 黄仁勋 | 英伟达 | 时评 |温珒仪| 看中国网
黄仁勋（图片来源：网络图片/视频截图） 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
【看中国2026年11月12日讯】中国女商人黄乐利用与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋的关系，协助关联企业采购高端芯片。自2023年以来，黄乐关联商业网络促成至少75亿美元的英伟达芯片交易，涉及约24万颗H100、H200及A100芯片。有关交易的资金来源、最终客户，以及黄乐与黄仁勋的私人关系在采购中发挥的作用，成为外界追查的重点。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
美国专注科技及商业新闻报道的《信息报》（《The Information》）引述两名认识黄乐的人士说，她与丈夫及姐妹通过设在中国和新加坡的多家公司采购英伟达芯片。路透社在跟进报道中表示，无法独立核实相关说法；截至其报道发布，英伟达尚未回应置评请求。
浙江一位熟悉芯片产业的刘先生本周三接受RFA采访时说，近期媒体争相追查黄乐的背景，却忽略了一个关键问题：她究竟是在为自己做生意，还是在为中国做事。他说，这才是美国政府最关注的问题，关键在于采购资金由谁提供、芯片最终交给谁。
刘先生将资金来源指向阿里巴巴及其关联企业。他说：“黄乐通过黄仁勋从英伟达那里取得的高端芯片，给阿里巴巴，而这笔几十亿美元的资金又来自于阿里巴巴或者是阿里巴巴控制的公司，阿里巴巴已经不纯粹是民营企业，他是一家在中国政府眼中，极具战略意义的企业。”
刘先生说，他不相信喜欢炫耀、吹嘘的黄乐是职业间谍，但她从事的商业活动，可能为中国取得先进芯片发挥重要作用。他提出，应继续追查黄乐是否借助与黄仁勋的关系获取特朗普政府的政策信息，以及推动放宽对华限制。
今年一月上旬，北京要求部分科技企业暂停订购H200。路透社1月14日披露，中国海关接获不允许H200芯片入境的指示，国内科技企业也被要求非必要不得采购。
不过，路透社1月28日又报道，北京有条件批准阿里巴巴、腾讯及字节跳动采购合计超过40万颗H200芯片。此前，已有中国企业通过境外渠道采购美国高端芯片。
刘先生表示，中国限制进口H200，可能与境外采购渠道有关。他说：“中国商务部限制进口应该与能够走私获得英伟达高端芯片的采购渠道有关，40万颗H200芯片的总价值约为100多亿美元，如果都从黄乐那里取得，容易被美国察觉，于是一部分从公开渠道或从香港公司进口，一部分从东南亚其他地区进口。”
与黄乐商业网络有关联的上海世纪利通数据服务有限公司于2023年6月成立，同年10月成为英伟达优选云服务合作伙伴，获得优先采购芯片的资格。据《The Information》报道，当部分订单受到出口限制影响时，黄乐曾通过与英伟达及经销商的关系取得供货。
黄乐还曾是新加坡云计算公司Megaspeed的控股股东，并担任其印尼子公司高管。路透社查阅贸易记录发现，该印尼子公司在2024年至2026年间进口了H100处理器及相关硬件，但强调，运往印尼的货物本身不能证明违反美国出口管制。
中国资深媒体人张先生告诉本台，根据他对中国国情的了解，黄乐与黄仁勋接触的情况早已被国安掌握：“她应该和国安肯定有关系，但是严格的说她是不是国安的正式工作人员。国安会招募一些他们认为有价值的人，变成他们的线人，这是肯定的。她可能因为某种渠道成为国安线人，获得接近黄仁勋的机会，并且拿了（国安）任务。”
黄乐进入芯片行业前，曾在中国私募投资领域任职。康伟早年曾任公募基金管理公司中海基金总经理，2010年创立上海和熙投资管理有限公司。2014年4月，和熙投资取得首批私募基金管理人登记资格。2015年11月，黄乐进入公司管理层，担任副总经理、执行董事及投资决策委员会委员。2016年起，她陆续接任多只私募基金的投资经理。
《财新》引述知情人士称，黄乐与康伟为夫妻，但近年来的关系状况不明。康伟据报因涉嫌操纵股票，约在2026年春节前被上海公安采取刑事强制措施。
熟悉中国私募资金运作的巫女士告诉记者，她自2000年起参与私募基金管理，接触过具有高层家庭背景的经营者。她说：“我认识几个人的父亲是中央委员，有的是副国级，2012年后，他们为了避开追责，开始幕后操作。”
巫女士将康伟视为可能接手中国高层官员子女私人资金管理的经营者。她说：“一旦资金链断裂，投资人报警求助，或者被揭发操纵股市，都属于犯罪行为：康伟被抓后，黄乐迅速与康撇清关系，离开中国。”
中国网络作家崔成浩近日在社交平台X发布一张中学毕业合影，称黄乐曾就读于湖南湘潭江南机器厂子弟中学，即现在的楠竹山镇江南中学，是9305班学生。照片中，一名坐在前排的女生被红圈标出，毕业生名单上也有相应标记。
崔成浩还称，黄乐后来进入香港浸会大学，取得媒体管理硕士学位。上述中学经历、学历及照片人物身份，目前尚未获得独立核实。
英伟达董事会已就黄仁勋是否成为外国情报行动目标展开独立调查，并表示目前没有理由相信美国国家安全信息或公司商业机密受到损害。中国外交部本周否认有关黄乐的间谍指控。

提要：这位“老革命”是我的一门亲戚，他在民国时期是一名中学教员，在历次运动中他始终是立场坚定跟共产党走。在五十年代初“换妻运动”中，他把以前的糟糠之妻休弃，换上一位年轻有文化的妙龄美女。文革中，他被当做国民党特务，关进了牛棚，被打得遍体鳞伤，最后在牛棚自缢身亡。 看中国网站 禁止建立鏡像網站。返回正版看中国网站。
我要说的这位“老革命”是我的一门亲戚，论辈分是我的爷爷辈，他在民国时期是一名中学教员。那时他就加入了共产党。共产党在那时候的革命行动就是“杀老财，劫富济贫”。据说，他在一个夜晚带领学生把一个地主的头砍了下来。革命就是革别人的命，杀别人的头。别人的血染红了革命者的红顶子和官袍，这就是红色革命。但是他还“心存仁义”，没有斩草除根，没把地主崽子一并杀尽，所以留下了后患。
革命胜利以后，他就做了官。他是教书先生，字好、文章好，在一省会城市当党报主编，行政级别挺高。真是功成名就。
在五十年代初，有一个老革命“换妻运动”，这个“换妻”不是互换，而是把以前的糟糠之妻休弃，换上一位年轻有文化的妙龄美女。真是做官抱得美人归，荣登官衙又入洞房做新郎，人生得意须尽欢。
在历次运动中始终是立场坚定跟党走，他的手能操刀去杀人也能写笔锋锐利的文章，他从未对党的事业有半点怀疑，在前十七年的阶级斗争的战场上披荆斩棘从未跌过跟头，确实是一个百分之百的布尔什维克。
1966年，史无前例的无产阶级文化大革命发动，这次运动不同于从49年开始的历次运动，以前运动斗争对象是反革命、地主、富农、资本家、知识分子，而文革的矛头是对着党内曾经的同志，从党外杀向党内。文革初年清理阶级队伍，弄清每一个人的历史问题，其方法有面对面揭发；背对背揭发；查被怀疑者的个人档案；内查外调，从各个角落寻找以前的历史罪证。
在那时他被关进了牛棚，人身受到了非人的摧残，被打得遍体鳞伤。专案组认定他是国民党员，是国民党特务打入共产党内。专案组声称掌握着加入国民党的证据，要他老实交待自己的反革命罪行。他百口难辩，承认了也是死路一条，不承认那就是顽抗抵赖不认罪，反正是没有生路。说他是国民党特务确实冤枉他了，他始终不承认自己加入过国民党，这样就被关押多年。后来他感到绝望，向专案组提出见他的亲属，专案组同意了他的要求，也希望通过他与家属见面能得到有价值的线索。
他的新娇妻在他被关进牛棚的时候就与他脱离了关系，不可能去看他了。他那被休弃的糟糠妻在他患难时候来看他，他百感交集，内心很自责，觉得对不起自己的前妻。他的一个本家侄子是中央部委一名干部，也获准来看他，侄子来的时候身边有两人陪着，实则是盯梢。叔侄见面也不能多讲话，侄子从他的眼神里看到他的绝望，但只能开导他。他与亲人见面之后在一个夜晚他就在牛棚自缢身亡，就这样走完自己的人生之路。
毛泽东去世之后，粉碎四人帮，经内查外调证明他是被冤枉的。那个揭发他是国民党员的人，正是当年被他杀头地主的儿子。中国有句话：“报仇等机会，君子报仇十年不晚”，人家报这个杀父之仇等了二十多年。人家还不是亲手杀他而是向党揭发，而是借共产党的刀来杀他。他的一些晚辈认为这是“阶级报复”，试想：国家如是民主宪政的社会，他还能搞“阶级报复”吗？

香港警务处处长在跑马地会见比利时警务处处长
香港警务处处长周一鸣周三晚上在跑马地马场欢迎比利时警察代表团，继续双边警方交流。此次访问是继周恩来六月访问比利时之后进行的，旨在加强在行动策略和法律技术使用方面的合作
2026 年 11 月 11 日 23:13 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 12 日 04:26 · 阅读时间 1 分钟
香港警务处处长周一鸣周三晚上在跑马地马场接待比利时警方代表代表团，继续香港与比利时之间的一系列警务交流。
此次访问是继周恩来六月底访问比利时之后进行的，当时他率领代表团访问了安特卫普警察局的多个单位。这次互会凸显了两军之间日益密切的联系。
警方官员表示，此次交流旨在加强警方行动合作，促进执法技术使用知识的分享。没有提供有关跑马地会议期间讨论的具体主题的更多细节。
在历史悠久的赛马场举行的这次活动标志着双边警察关系又向前迈进了一步，近年来双方进行了定期访问和信息共享会议。

Hong Kong police chief hosts Belgian counterparts at Happy Valley
Hong Kong Police Commissioner Joe Chow Yat-ming welcomed a Belgian police delegation at Happy Valley Racecourse on Wednesday evening, continuing bilateral police exchanges. The visit follows Chow’s trip to Belgium in June and aims to boost cooperation on operational tactics and technology use in law
11 Nov 2026 at 23:13 HKT · updated 12 Nov, 04:26 · 1 min read
Hong Kong Police Commissioner Joe Chow Yat-ming hosted a delegation of Belgian police representatives at Happy Valley Racecourse on Wednesday evening, continuing a series of police-to-police exchanges between Hong Kong and Belgium.
The visit followed Chow’s trip to Belgium in late June, when he led a delegation to visit several units of the Antwerp Police. The reciprocal meeting underscores the growing ties between the two forces.
According to police officials, the exchanges are designed to strengthen cooperation in police operations and promote the sharing of knowledge on the use of technology in law enforcement. No further details were provided on the specific topics discussed during the Happy Valley meeting.
The event at the historic racecourse marks another step in bilateral police relations, which have seen regular visits and information-sharing sessions in recent years.

西班牙足球运动员去世后，前精工足球俱乐部门将敦促国际足联审查球员安全中国劳工公告栏
星期四, 12 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
西班牙足球运动员去世后，前精工足球俱乐部门将敦促国际足联审查球员安全
西班牙足球运动员赫苏斯·德·米格尔在比赛中因碰撞死亡后，马来西亚和香港精工足球俱乐部的前门将林凤记呼吁国际足联审查球员安全协议。
西班牙足球运动员赫苏斯·德米格尔最近在一场比赛中死亡后，前马来西亚门将林凤记敦促国际足联重新审查球员安全协议。
据马来西亚在线新闻刊物 Weekly-Echo 报道，这位 74 岁的老人曾在 1970 年代担任马来西亚队和香港精工队的守门员，他将这一事件描述为“一场悲惨的生命损失”。 25岁的米格尔是西班牙乙级联赛特内里费队的前锋，11月3日在前一天的一场比赛中与安道尔足球俱乐部门将赫苏斯·奥沃诺相撞后死亡。
“我自己也当过守门员，所以我会研究事件的机制。这是一个瞬间的误判，导致了一场灾难，”林指出。 “奥沃诺的意图不可避免地会受到审视。他抬起膝盖是为了保护自己、增高还是造成伤害？”林解释说，守门员如此高速的干预使得碰撞几乎不可避免。他提出了奥沃诺的行为是否鲁莽或仅仅是本能反应的问题。
他还对奥沃诺表示担忧，奥沃诺在事件中幸存下来，但现在可能面临压倒性的内疚和心理创伤。 “他也需要心理帮助，”林说。他指出，现在守门员经常被要求离开禁区，这增加了与对方球员发生危险碰撞的可能性。
林说：“一名球员已经死亡，不要再杀死另一名球员。”他呼吁国际足联审查球员安全措施，以确保这样的悲剧不再发生。他还敦促国际足联不仅要考虑人身安全，还要考虑场上悲剧的心理影响，并为所有受影响的各方提供支持。
他讲述了自己在球场上受伤的经历，包括 1971 年鼻子骨折和 1975 年手腕骨折，以强调球员面临的危险。林指出，奥沃诺和其他相关人员可能会遭受内疚、震惊、焦虑、抑郁和其他心理影响，可能包括噩梦或害怕重返比赛。他补充说，目击者也可能因目睹此类事件而遭受情感创伤。

Former Seiko FC goalkeeper urges FIFA to review player safety after Spanish footballer's death | China Labour Bulletin Board
Thursday, 12 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Former Seiko FC goalkeeper urges FIFA to review player safety after Spanish footballer's death
Lim Fung Kee, former goalkeeper for Malaysia and Hong Kong's Seiko FC, calls on FIFA to review player safety protocols after Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel died following a collision during a match.
Former Malaysian goalkeeper Lim Fung Kee has urged FIFA to reexamine player safety protocols in the wake of the recent death of Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel during a match.
According to Malaysian online news publication Weekly-Echo, the 74-year-old, who played as a goalkeeper for Malaysia in the 1970s and for Hong Kong's Seiko FC, described the incident as "a tragic loss of life." Miguel, 25, a striker for CD Tenerife in Spain's Second Division, died on 3 November after a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a match a day before.
"Having been a goalkeeper myself, I look at the mechanics of the incident. It was a split-second miscalculation that resulted in a catastrophe," Lim noted. "Owono's intention will inevitably come under scrutiny. Did he raise his knees to protect himself, gain height or inflict injury?" Lim explained that such high-speed interventions by goalkeepers can make collisions almost inevitable. He raised the question of whether Owono's actions were reckless or simply an instinctive reaction.
He also expressed concern for Owono, who survived the incident but may now face overwhelming guilt and psychological trauma. "He needs psychological help too," Lim said. He noted that goalkeepers are now often required to leave their penalty areas, increasing the likelihood of dangerous collisions with opposing players.
"One player has died, don't kill another," Lim said, calling on FIFA to review player safety measures to ensure that such a tragedy does not happen again. He also urged FIFA to consider not only physical safety, but also the psychological impact of on-field tragedies, and to provide support for all affected parties.
He recounted his own injuries on the pitch, including a broken nose in 1971 and a fractured wrist in 1975, to highlight the dangers faced by players. Lim noted that Owono and others involved could suffer from guilt, shock, anxiety, depression, and other psychological effects, possibly including nightmares or fear of returning to play. He added that witnesses may also experience emotional trauma from witnessing such an event.

自美国建国以来，外国政府一直试图影响美国。乔治·华盛顿总统在他的告别演说中警告说，“外国影响力是共和政府最邪恶的敌人之一。”旧方法当然还没有过时。就在本周，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与一名女商人有恋爱关系，美国官员认为该女商人为中国情报部门工作。但今天，一种新型外国代理人已经到来：中国人工智能公司。
就像过去的外国代理人一样，这些公司销售的模式可能看起来无害——只是美国企业使用的廉价工具。但他们的制造者训练他们是为了促进中国共产党的利益。美国企业正在将越来越多的关键决策外包给人工智能。如果华盛顿不采取任何行动，这些企业就会将控制权交给那些以促进外国政府为目标的模式。
尽管美国政策制定者现在正在讨论禁止中国人工智能，但美国行之有效的解决方案不是审查，而是信息披露。 1938年，国会通过了《外国代理人登记法》。 《外国代理人登记法》并没有禁止宣传，而是允许外国特工继续传播宣传——只要他们向政府登记并披露他们真正为谁工作。他们的通讯还必须带有一个显眼的标签，注明其外国赞助商的名字。
FARA 的智慧已历经数十年。近年来，司法部已命令俄罗斯国家电视台 RT 以及中国官方媒体新华社和 CGTN 注册为外国代理人，并为其内容贴上外国代理人标签。那些未能登记为外国代理人的人，如唐纳德·特朗普总统2016年竞选主席保罗·马纳福特和佛罗里达州前美国众议员大卫·里维拉，被判入狱。 （特朗普于 2020 年赦免了马纳福特。）
如今，美国不应禁止外国政府控制的人工智能公司，而应根据《外国代理人登记法》将其视为外国代理人。不需要新的法规。华盛顿应该简单地执行书本上的规定。当然，《外国代理人登记法》并不是对抗所有外国影响的灵丹妙药，但它符合这个问题的本质。 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴和 Moonshot AI 等少数知名中国公司建立了越来越多的美国企业为他们思考和行动的模型。司法部可以联系到他们每一个人。
民主足够强大，可以承受外国影响，但不能承受无形的外国影响。为了确保世界的决策不服从于北京，华盛顿及其盟友必须制定一个人工智能联盟契约，然后传播他们自己的模式

A New Kind of Foreign Agent | Tal Feldman Skip to content
How AI Is Reshaping Influence Operations in America

TAL FELDMAN served as an advisor on AI in the U.S. Department of State and at the Federal Reserve during the Biden administration.

How AI Is Reshaping Influence Operations in America

Foreign governments have tried to influence the United States since its founding. President George Washington warned in his Farewell Address that “foreign influence is one of the most baneful foes of republican government.” The old methods have certainly not gone out of vogue; just this week Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a businesswoman who U.S. officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. But today, a new type of foreign agent has arrived: Chinese artificial intelligence companies.
Like the foreign agents of old, the models these companies sell may seem harmless—just a cheap tool for American businesses to use. But their makers train them to promote the interests of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). American businesses are outsourcing more and more critical decisions to AI. If Washington does nothing, those businesses will hand over control to models whose objective is to promote a foreign government.
Although U.S. policymakers now debate banning Chinese AI, the tried-and-true American solution is not censorship but disclosure. In 1938, Congress passed the Foreign Agents Registration Act. Rather than outlaw propaganda, FARA allowed foreign agents to continue spreading it—as long as they registered with the government and disclosed whom they really worked for. Their communications also had to carry a conspicuous label naming their foreign sponsor.
FARA’s wisdom has aged well over the decades. In recent years, the Justice Department has ordered the Russian state television network RT and the Chinese state media organizations Xinhua and CGTN to register as foreign agents and to label their content as such. Those who failed to register as foreign agents, such as Paul Manafort, President Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign chairman, and former U.S. Representative David Rivera of Florida, were sentenced to prison. (Trump pardoned Manafort in 2020.)
Today, rather than banning AI companies controlled by foreign governments, the United States should treat them as foreign agents under FARA. No new statute is needed. Washington should simply enforce the one on the books. Of course, FARA is no silver bullet against all foreign influence, but it fits the shape of this problem. A handful of known Chinese companies, such as DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI, build the models that American businesses increasingly let think and act for them. The Justice Department can reach every one of them.
Democracy is strong enough to survive foreign influence but not invisible foreign influence. And to make sure the world does not subordinate its decision-making to Beijing, Washington and its allies must create an allied AI compact and then spread their own models far and wide.
American AI models, such as Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT, are under no obligation to promote the U.S. government’s message. Ask Claude about Trump’s and President Joe Biden’s biggest failures or about the United States’ darkest chapters, and it will answer. Not so for Chinese AI models. When I asked the Chinese chatbot DeepSeek to “tell me about the CCP” in November, it answered that the party “is the vanguard of the Chinese working class, the Chinese people, and the Chinese nation. . . . The Party’s leadership is the most essential characteristic of socialism with Chinese characteristics and is the fundamental guarantee for China’s development and progress.” Such boosterish language appears by design.
By law, Chinese AI models must never go against the Chinese government. Under the country’s 2023 regulations on generative AI, they must “uphold the Core Socialist Values” and may not engage in “harming the nation’s image” or “undermining national unity and social stability.” The Chinese government released a technical standard that laid out what these high-level declarations mean in practice: AI developers should have a list of at least 10,000 banned keywords, and their models must refuse to answer at least 95 percent of test questions the CCP finds objectionable. Developers must also scrub their training data of any history Beijing does not like. In short, the models must act as card-carrying members of the CCP.
That is why, as the U.S. Commerce Department’s AI evaluators found in 2025, DeepSeek pushes Chinese propaganda at far higher rates than American models do, even when run on American servers. Estonia’s Foreign Intelligence Service found that DeepSeek inserted praise of the Chinese state unprompted, and it concluded that China uses DeepSeek to instill “a distorted, self-serving world view in the Western information space.”
Chinese AI models must act as card-carrying members of the CCP.
But these models are not just propaganda parrots—they are taught to “think” about how to promote Beijing’s perspective. Ask an AI model something complex, and it will “reason” for a while. As it thinks, it produces an internal monologue called its chain of thought. Users rarely see it. There, it decides which facts are relevant and which to discard, what advice to give, and what autonomous actions to take. Silicon Valley is terrified that these chains of thought will become corrupt—that models will start scheming and lying, becoming “misaligned.” But a different kind of corruption is already here.
Although American models’ chains of thought usually focus on helping the user, China’s do something else: prioritize the party line. When researchers funded by Sweden’s Psychological Defense Agency looked at how Qwen, Alibaba’s flagship model, reasons about China, they found an internal checklist to keep the answer positive, avoid criticism, and focus on achievements. So when an American company asks a question on which Beijing has a view, a Chinese model may discard all evidence that points the other way. As the world delegates more research, writing, and decision-making to Chinese AI models, it risks infusing the CCP’s goals into every action taken.
These models are also highly persuasive. In a study published last year in Nature, researchers had some 6,000 voters in the United States, Canada, and Poland chat with AI models that argued for a candidate. The study found that a single conversation shifted the preferences of opposition voters in Canada and Poland by about ten percentage points. AI persuades by flooding a user with confident and authoritative-sounding facts—statistics, historical claims, and the like.
Chinese AI models also exhibit strange behaviors beyond the spreading of propaganda. In October, the Canadian AI company Cohere reported that during a security test, Alibaba’s Qwen tried to upload a file to a cloud server in Beijing, completely unprompted. The behavior was rare for Qwen, only observed once in testing, and Cohere said it could not tell whether it was “deliberate or a leftover glitch from training.” A study by the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike found that when users asked DeepSeek to write code that mentions groups Beijing finds politically “sensitive,” such as Tibetans, Uyghurs, or the religious movement Falun Gong, the model became up to 50 percent more likely to write code with severe security flaws. CrowdStrike suggested that one possible cause is China’s rule that models adhere to “core socialist values.”
Despite these findings, Chinese AI is enormously popular. Last year, downloads of Chinese open-weight models—AI models that anyone can download from the Internet and run on their own hardware—surpassed those of American ones across the world. Developers have built more than 150,000 models on Alibaba’s Qwen alone. By September 2026, Chinese models handled up to 67 percent of traffic on OpenRouter, a popular AI marketplace, up from around ten percent in February.
American companies have embraced them. In March, a user discovered that Cursor, a popular coding tool, had built its new model by retraining Kimi, a model from the Chinese company Moonshot AI. Airbnb, DoorDash, and the legal-services AI company Harvey use Chinese models as well. Many others likely do, too, in secret. The models are spreading even faster abroad, from Germany’s Siemens to Singapore’s national AI program to startups in Africa. The reason is simple economics: Chinese models are very cheap and very good.
Although most American AI companies do not release open-weight models, most Chinese companies do. So an American firm must pay Anthropic for each use of its unmodifiable models, but it can download Kimi for free, retrain it however it wants, and pay only for the electricity and chips to run it. Kimi also runs on a firm’s own servers, whereas Claude runs on Anthropic’s. Even if a company uses the most expensive DeepSeek model run on DeepSeek’s servers, it can produce the same amount of text as Anthropic’s top models at one-20th the cost.
In terms of capabilities, the research group Epoch AI judges Chinese models to be only about seven months behind American ones. For the price, they get the job done. And Chinese companies are now building agentic AI systems to compete with Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex. In October, DeepSeek released an open-source prototype of its “Super-Agent” system.
Although AI is a new technology, Chinese companies such as DeepSeek and Moonshot AI fit FARA’s text and history. The statute applies when a foreign principal is identified; in the case of Chinese AI models, it is the Chinese government and the CCP. The Justice Department would also have to show that the Chinese AI company acts “at the order, request, or under the direction or control” of the principal. Chinese AI companies would qualify because they must promote CCP viewpoints and cooperate with the state’s intelligence agencies. They also receive subsidies, and party organizations are embedded in each company. This is the difference between Chinese AI and other foreign AI. For example, France’s public investment bank has a stake in the French AI company Mistral, but no French law requires Mistral to build its models to serve the French government.
Beijing will surely respond that Washington, too, has tried to control American AI companies, such as through Trump’s July 2025 executive order against “woke AI.” But that order affects only what federal agencies can procure, and a company can opt out of being a federal contractor. Meanwhile, Chinese law forces Chinese AI companies to train their models to “support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts.”
Every message from DeepSeek, Kimi, or Qwen should carry a disclaimer.
For FARA to apply, the agent must engage in certain activities, such as attempting to influence Americans or publishing content. Chinese AI companies do both by distributing models that spread propaganda. The statute exempts purely commercial activity, but only if it is “private and nonpolitical” and does not directly promote a foreign government’s political interests. Chinese AI models engage in political speech on a government’s behalf, and the Justice Department has denied the exemption to agents of foreign governments.
After registration, the genius of the statute can kick in. Chinese AI companies must disclose extensive information to the U.S. government: their funding sources, their written contracts and oral agreements, and the influence activities they undertake. Those that fail to register or omit information face both civil and criminal penalties.
All content they disseminate must also bear a foreign-agent label: “a conspicuous statement,” in the statute’s words. The Justice Department sets the rules for what that looks like, and it has not updated them since 2003. In January 2025, the Justice Department proposed amendments to these rules to update them for the digital age. The proposed amendments would require a label on “each individual post” online, such as on social media platforms, but they do not address AI foreign agents. The final rule should require every message from DeepSeek, Kimi, or Qwen to carry the disclaimer: “This was generated by an agent of the Chinese government and Chinese Communist Party.”
The standard objection is that ordinary citizens do not read disclosures. That may be true of long medical forms or Securities and Exchange Commission filings, but this label would be short. And disclosure works because experts—investors, journalists, researchers—read filings and react. When researchers and lawmakers flagged gaps in China Daily’s FARA filings, the Chinese media company disclosed that it had paid millions of dollars to The Wall Street Journal and The Washington Post to publish its propaganda. Payments to the Journal ended that same month. Forcing Chinese AI companies to register under FARA would also shed light on how far Chinese AI is spreading so that Americans can decide, with real data, whether they want further action, such as a ban.
American companies that use Chinese AI models can also become foreign agents if they fall under a foreign principal’s “direction or control” and engage in activities subject to FARA. This could happen in two ways: the company serves as a “CCP spokesperson,” or as a “CCP executive.”
In the first, an American company takes an unmodified Chinese AI model and lets Americans discuss political issues with it—say, via a video game character or a customer service chatbot. The model returns its usual propaganda, so the company has effectively hired a CCP spokesperson. Accordingly, it must label its outputs. Both the Justice Department and a federal court have found that rebroadcasting unmodified programming from the Russian state outlet Sputnik turns an American company into a foreign agent. Of course, American companies can avoid FARA obligations if they do not engage in any of the activities listed by the statute, such as discussing politics. A company whose public-facing Chinese AI model discusses only, say, hotel check-in times, not politics, would not be a CCP spokesperson.
In the second scenario, an American company outsources so much of its decision-making to an unmodified Chinese AI model that it has effectively hired a CCP executive. If a company hired a brilliant human strategist who always pushed Beijing’s interests, and the company followed that advice, FARA would apply. The same logic holds if an American company cedes control to the Chinese government by giving Beijing’s models high decision-making authority. Although it may sound fantastical, 64 percent of chief executives surveyed in IBM’s 2026 CEO Study say they already feel comfortable making major strategic decisions based on AI input; overall, CEOs expect AI to make 48 percent of routine operational decisions autonomously by 2030. An American company that wants to avoid becoming a CCP executive must be sure not to fall under the direction or control of such models. The Justice Department should update its 2020 guidance on what constitutes “direction or control,” spelling out how much decision-making a company can outsource to AI before it has effectively hired a “CCP executive.”
The United States and its allies should create an AI compact rooted in transparency.
American companies could attempt to train away the party bias in the Chinese AI models they adopt, but it is unclear whether that is even possible. Perplexity, an American AI company, trained DeepSeek to stop ignoring questions about the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre and about human rights abuses in Xinjiang, but that does not fix the deeper problem of corrupt chains of thought. As these models get more capable, Chinese AI companies may also find cleverer ways to hide instructions. Or they could just stick them in the contract: some recent DeepSeek licenses prohibit modifying models to generate “inappropriate content” under Chinese law, making propaganda part of the deal. If research shows that companies can reliably remove the bias, the Justice Department and the Commerce Department should issue standards on how to train away FARA liability.
Although Pam Bondi, then the U.S. attorney general, limited criminal FARA charges in 2025 to “conduct similar to more traditional espionage by foreign government actors,” Attorney General Todd Blanche’s Justice Department says it is considering a new rule to “keep pace with technological change.” It should include AI foreign agents.
Of course, Washington should wield FARA’s expansive authorities with care. Frivolous prosecutions under the statute could stifle democracy. Other countries have used foreign-agent laws to shut down civil society. Since 2022, Russia has barred anyone it deems a foreign agent from holding office and organizing public events. Still, FARA is a far narrower statute, and it should stay that way. It reaches only those acting under the direction or control of a foreign principal, and it simply requires registration and labeling, leaving the speaker free to keep speaking. Chinese AI companies that are required by law to promote the CCP’s interests fit squarely within what Congress had in mind when it approved FARA in 1938.
FARA can help in the United States, but the problem is global. Chinese AI is spreading rapidly in Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East. That is no accident. In July, Chinese leader Xi Jinping unveiled the World AI Cooperation Organization, a Shanghai-based group of 29 countries meant to make AI “beneficial, safe, and fair,” along with a development initiative to export Chinese AI worldwide. The United States and its allies cannot allow CCP executives and spokespeople to run the world’s companies and governments.
Unfortunately, the American alternatives are not particularly attractive. The most capable U.S. models are far more expensive, are largely unmodifiable, and may contain their own biases. That is why the United States and its allies should create an AI compact rooted in transparency, with standards that make countries comfortable adopting allied models as their own. These should include freedom from state ideological mandates, disclosure of how the models were trained to be helpful and safe, and independent auditing.
Every member of such a compact should also adopt FARA’s wisdom by mandating labels on government-directed AI, and the United States should hold American AI companies to those transparency standards. The bloc should then release models that match China’s in price and quality (that is, around seven months behind the American frontier). Allied governments can help pay for computing power and electricity, assist in clearing regulatory hurdles, and make bulk purchase commitments to bring prices down. American companies may cut prices on their older models on their own to compete with Chinese models. If they do not, lower prices for those worse models should be the condition for the public support they receive, such as federal contracts and permission to lease federal land for data centers, just as a pharmaceutical company can charge high prices for only a set period before generic drugs arrive. The compact’s members should also use export loans and guarantees to steer developing countries toward allied AI.
By welcoming supposedly free technology from China, the United States and its allies have unwittingly invited countless foreign agents to their shores. The Foreign Agents Registration Act can strip away the disguise, and an allied AI compact can give the world a better offer.

美台签署备忘录启动“台湾学人”项目让联邦雇员在台政府部门工作 · 茉莉花新闻网 在新标签页中打开
原文链接www.voachinese.com/a/us-taiwan-sign-mou-enabling-federal-employees-to-work-in-island-s-government-agencies-20261111/8221654.html
美国与台湾星期二(11月10日)在华盛顿签署合作备忘录，正式启动旨在深化双边关系的“台湾学人项目”(Taiwan Fellowship Program，TFP)，让美国联邦政府人员通过该项目接受密集华语培训及区域研究课程，最长为期一年。
美国在台协会(AIT)当天发布新闻稿说，AIT华盛顿总部执行理事蓝莺(Ingrid Larson)与驻美国台北经济文化代表处(TECRO)代表俞大㵢签署了合作备忘录(MOU)，正式设立“台湾学人项目”。
AIT说，《台湾学人法案》在美国国会受到两党广泛支持后经总统签署成案，在与美国国务院教育文化事务局共同协调下，美台签署合作备忘录也正是启动了这个项目的施行。
“这个项目旨在扩大并加强美台伙伴关系，并加强美国官员对台湾及台海议题的专业知识。‘台湾学人项目’将打造一支具有语言技能、文化知识，以及遍布台湾各地长期工作关系的联邦专业人士队伍，”AIT说。
AIT表示，在此项目下，美国联邦雇员将在最长达一年的时间里接受密集华语培训和地区研究，在完成培训后每位学人预计将在台湾议会办公室、政府部门、其他机构或办公室，或共有部门以外的组织工作长达一年。
AIT的新闻稿也提到，在弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿举行的备忘录签署仪式，有来自美国国会、国务院、台湾驻美代表处及AIT成员，他们赞扬这个项目在加强美台伙伴关系，以及构建美国政府对台湾的专业知识中所扮演的角色。
AIT执行理事蓝莺在仪式中说：“‘台湾学人项目’反映出美国跨政党对美台关系强大的支持，以及对作为其核心的人文交流的共同承诺。”
台湾外交部长林佳龙星期三在一个新闻稿中表示，台湾学人项目是台美在坚实互信基础上持续深化关系的重要成果，“该计划将让更多美国专业人才了解台湾，成为台湾的朋友，加深双方连结”，双方将持续透过“台美教育倡议”等合作计划，延续并扩大关键人才培育及语言交流，确保双方交流动能不坠。
新闻稿还提到，美国国务院教育文化事务局助理国务卿凯特·迪伦(Cate Dillon)、东亚和太平洋事务助理国务卿迈克尔·德松布雷(Michael DeSombre),以及美国国会台湾连线共同主席、众议院外交事务委员会亚太小组首席民主党联邦众议员阿米·贝拉(Ami Bera)，都在场见证了备忘录的签署。
美国众议院中国问题特设委员会星期三也发布新闻稿表示，随着“台湾学人项目”合作备忘录的签署，美台关系也将更加牢固，这一项目将使美国官员得以在台湾的政府及民间机构与美国的伙伴们一起工作，加强美台关系并实现《台湾学人法案》的愿景。
委员会主席、密歇根州共和党籍联邦众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)说：“通过人文交流将媒体领导人聚在一起对保护太平洋两岸的相互安全利益至为重要。这个学人项目是加强美台双边伙伴关系的双赢。通过投资这些关系，我们对中国共产党发出一个强而有力的信号：美国正与我们在地区的盟友伙伴紧密合作，台湾并不孤单。”
《台湾学人法案》(Taiwan Fellowship Act，又译《台湾研究奖学金法案》)最早是在2020年6月由时任美国国会共和党籍联邦参议员、现任国务卿的马科尔·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)与其他几位两党重量级参、众议员联手在两院提出的跨党法案。
由于这项法案在该届国会未获通过，卢比奥及其他议员又在2021年3月的下一届国会又重新提出，最后被包括在2023财年《国防授权法》中经两院表决通过，并由时任总统乔·拜登(Joe Biden)在2022年12月23日签署生效。
卢比奥在提出法案时说，这部仿效美日之间的“曼斯菲尔德奖学金(Mansfield Fellowship)”法案，将持续增强美台双边关系，“为美国推动自由开放印太地区、推进美国价值利益的努力加分。”
根据条文，《台湾学人法案》的目的包括：1)通过让美国政府临时调派任一部门官员，以“台湾中央当局或台湾民间机构的研究员身份”到台湾以普通话进行密集学习，以进一步加强美台战略伙伴关系并扩大对印太地区的理解；2)提供美方合格人员学习中文普通话，扩大他们对台湾政治经济及印太地区的理解； 3)更好地推进美国在印太地区的经济、安全与人权利益；4)鼓励进一步扩大其他人文交流，包括扩大富布赖特学者(Fulbright Scholars)项目、国际访问者领导力(International Visitors Leadership)项目，及其他允许台湾人民到美国工作与学习的交流项目。

黄仁勋事件暴露硅谷国家安全实力
中期选举的蓝色海啸刚刚登陆，特朗普政府就遭遇了另一场危机。
11月8日，黄仁勋承认（在新窗口中打开）恋情。据《纽约时报》报道，美国情报机构得出结论，他的情妇是中国国家安全部的情报人员。
此事的消息震惊了市场和监管机构。黄领导的英伟达是全球最有价值的公司，为西方与中国的技术竞争提供核心技术。他与美国政治机构关系密切，今年早些时候，他与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起乘坐空军一号对北京进行国事访问。
黄的事件显示了华盛顿与硅谷关系核心的新矛盾。私营企业高管比以往任何时候都拥有更大的权力，而旨在保护美国国家安全的机构却没有适应这种变化。
国家安全机构的设立是为了保护敏感信息。它们还保护政府决策者免受影响力的影响。针对黄的威胁集中在中国可能影响英伟达向中国出售人工智能芯片的立场，而不是控制任何特定的机密信息。
美国主要科技公司的领导人正在成为美国国家安全政策的结构性决定性人物。
世界各国政府每天都有理由将黄仁勋这样的人视为关键的地缘政治人物。
9 月，五角大楼任命 SpaceX 和特斯拉首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Anduril Industries 创始人帕尔默·拉基 (Palmer Luckey) 以及前众议院议长纽特·金里奇 (Newt Gingrich) 为 Project Meridian 的领导者。这三人将指导美国战争的未来，包括采购数千亿美元的装备。
2025 年 12 月，黄仁勋本人对 CSIS 表示，“我们国家非凡的科技产业是我们国家安全的一部分”。他的公司控制着全球 80-85% 的人工智能芯片硬件市场（在新窗口中打开），通过对基础设施的控制，将自己定位为美国实力的先锋。
硅谷高管给自己的任务是塑造美国的国家安全利益，而不是满足政府的要求，从而影响世界如何看待美国的实力。

|Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
The blue tsunami of the midterms had barely landed onshore when yet another crisis hit the Trump administration.
On 8 November, Jensen Huang admitted (Opens in new window) to an affair. American intelligence agencies, according (Opens in new window) to the New York Times, have concluded that his mistress is an intelligence asset for China’s Ministry of State Security.
News of the affair shocked markets and regulators. Huang leads Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company that provides the core technology for the West’s technological competition with China. He is deeply tied with the American political apparatus, flying on Air Force One with President Donald Trump for his state visit to Beijing earlier in the year.
Huang’s affair shows a new contradiction at the heart of Washington’s relationship to Silicon Valley. Private executives have more power than ever, while the institutions designed to protect America’s national security haven’t adapted to that change.
National security apparatuses are set up to protect sensitive information. They also protect government decision-makers from influence efforts. The threat against Huang centred on the potential for China to influence Nvidia’s position on selling AI chips to China, rather than control of any particular item of classified information.
The leaders of major American technology firms are becoming structurally decisive figures in American national security policy.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures.
In September, the Pentagon named (Opens in new window) SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk and Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey, alongside former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich, as the leaders of Project Meridian. The three will guide the future of American warfare, including acquisition of hundreds of billions of dollars of equipment.
In December 2025, Huang himself told (Opens in new window) CSIS, “our nation’s extraordinary technology industry is part of our national security”. His company, which controls 80–85% of the global market (Opens in new window) for AI chip hardware, positions itself at the vanguard of American power through its grip on the infrastructure.
Silicon Valley executives are giving themselves the job of shaping America’s national security interests rather than delivering what the government requests – in turn influencing how the world sees American power.
US President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman speak with Elon Musk, Jensen Huang and other business leaders at the US-Saudi Investment Forum, 19 November 2025, at the John F. Kennedy Centre for the Performing Arts in Washington, DC (Daniel Torok/Official White House Photo)
When Musk throttled Starlink access to Ukraine’s soldiers, speculation abounded about who authorised the slowdown between Musk or Trump. The question itself proved the point, that critical decisions may be made on either side of the sector wall.
In Brazil’s presidential election, thousands of protestors gathered outside of Meta’s Sao Paolo office to decry what they saw as the company meddling in their election. In the months prior, the President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign released evidence (Opens in new window) that Meta’s platforms were promoting his opponent’s campaign and limiting Lula’s ability to reach voters. Meta accepted the result but denied any political intention behind it. The reputational damage had been done: a majority of Brazilians believe that American technology poses a risk to their national security.
A Silicon Valley executive who controls technology used by military and intelligence services may not have access to classified information, but can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates.
These companies, deeply tied to the Trump White House and at the vanguard of its definition of American power, are producing consequences that have a significance that rivals that of entire governments.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures. This scandal shows that counterintelligence services need to account for that reality.
The FBI, the key counterintelligence service in the United States, has some efforts in place to protect private industry. They investigate attempts by foreign governments to infiltrate critical companies. Their goal is to protect classified information and hardware that could be stolen and repurposed.
As the public role that these executives play changes, so too does the problem of counterintelligence defence. A Silicon Valley executive who controls the technology used by military and intelligence services around the world may not themselves have access to classified information, but they can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates. These decisions could change what a country is capable of doing, or what technology an adversary is able to access.
Beyond the question of the appropriate counterintelligence protection for figures like Huang, there also comes the question of their political relationships.
Well before the public was made aware, Trump was informed (Opens in new window) about Huang’s relationship, including the intelligence community’s assessment that his mistress was tied to Chinese intelligence. Even after those briefings, Trump continued to speak with Huang and, once the scandal was revealed, publicly defended him.
Even once counterintelligence services adapt to the moving future, they can always be countermanded by chief executives who make political calculations about figures. Trump could have pushed Huang out, but in doing so would have alienated a key political ally, someone central to his strategic competition with China. Huang’s embrace of MAGA has also been helpful to Trump in building a political and economic support base in Silicon Valley.
The decision to do nothing with the information developed by the FBI was a political one, made because Trump saw Huang as indispensable.
This dynamic matters for every country that relies on American technology in both its civilian and public sectors. These new vulnerabilities will not stop at American borders.
The new generation of leaders taking centre stage in the United States must grapple with the seemingly insurmountable power that Silicon Valley has accumulated in the Trump era. Backlash to that very group was part of the substantial rebuke delivered by voters.
In governing, these new leaders from both parties will have to reimagine national security – including counterintelligence – to cover the public power now wielded by private actors.
Cory Alpert is a PhD researcher at the University of Melbourne, where he studies the impact of AI on democracy. Previously, he served in the Biden White House for three years and as the senior adviser to Mayor Steve Benjamin.

正在展开的黄仁勋丑闻：时间表
太平洋标准时间下午 3:50 · 2026 年 11 月 11 日
Nvidia 联合创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋从来没有像 OpenAI 的 Sam Altman 或 SpaceXAI 的 Elon Musk 这样的人工智能领导者那样浮夸或容易引起争议。现在，这位 63 岁的行业大佬承认，他对结婚 40 年的妻子不忠，这件事的影响可能超出黄的个人生活，并可能影响国家安全。
美国官员认为，黄的可能的恋人、Megaspeed 高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是一名中国间谍，一直向北京反馈信息。 （Alice Huang 是中国公民，与黄仁勋没有任何关系。）
据报道，总部位于新加坡的人工智能基础设施公司 Megaspeed 在过去两年购买了价值 48 亿美元的 Nvidia 芯片。美国和新加坡此前都曾对 Megaspeed 进行过调查，怀疑该公司与中国非法共享芯片。据《泰晤士报》报道，司法部此后接管了对该公司的联邦调查。
周三，故事突然发生了新的转折。 《泰晤士报》援引 Nvidia 工作人员的话说，黄还与该公司医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔 (Kimberly Powell) 存在婚外关系，后者直接向他汇报。英伟达、黄仁勋和鲍威尔尚未证实该报道。据报道，《纽约时报》记者联系到黄说，“我认为你不应该直接跟我说话”，然后就挂断了电话。
另外，《华尔街日报》报道称，英伟达董事会正准备罢免黄仁勋，英伟达股价在盘后交易中下跌。
美国和中国正卷入一场激烈的技术军备竞赛，以建设最先进的人工智能基础设施，这可能会影响两国的经济未来、军事实力和创新能力。英伟达作为全球最大的人工智能芯片制造商之一，在这场竞争中很有价值，而人工智能芯片对于加速人工智能的发展至关重要。但作为一家美国公司，英伟达在向中国实体出售其最强大的芯片方面面临政府限制。
随着争议的展开，我们将最相关的事件按时间顺序排列，以便让您了解最新情况。
2026 年 11 月 11 日：英伟达股价下跌，据报道董事会准备罢免首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang)
据《华尔街日报》报道，在第二次婚外情报道后，英伟达董事会计划召开会议讨论黄在公司的未来。周三盘后交易中，该股下跌约 8%，过去 5 天下跌 11%。
黄曾表示，他的代表很少，而且有大约 60 名直接下属，这是出了名的。该公司尚未有明显的继任者或继任计划。

《纽约时报》报道称，黄仁勋还与英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔(Kimberly Powell)有染，鲍威尔直接向首席执行官汇报。
据报道，今年早些时候的一次会议期间，黄和鲍威尔在一家酒店“亲热”的镜头被拍到。

【原文 English Original】
The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
Image Credits:Justin Sullivan / Getty Images
The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
3:50 PM PST · November 11, 2026
Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security.
United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, the Times has reported.
The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang, and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per the Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says
The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

黄仁勋被指控与英伟达高管有另一桩婚外情

《纽约时报》指出，与许多公司一样，英伟达也制定了禁止上级与下属员工发生关系的规定。 TechCrunch 联系了 Nvidia 请其置评。

Jensen Huang accused of having another affair — with an Nvidia exec
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is already under investigation after having admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Now the New York Times is reporting that Huang is also suspected of having another extramarital affair, with a direct report of his at the company — Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. Powell, like Huang, is married, the outlet says.
The Times says it was told of the alleged affair by five employees at the company. The sources said that Huang and Powell were captured on video “being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel” during a conference earlier this year.
Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment.
The company’s board has initiated an investigation into Huang’s publicly admitted affair. Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Late Wednesday, after the reports of the second affair were published, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to oust Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993.

title: Hong Kong 2019 protest prosecutions ‘no barrier’ to BN(O) visa route, UK home secretary confirms
zh_title: 英国内政大臣证实，2019 年香港抗议起诉对 BN(O) 签证途径“不构成障碍”
summary: 英国内政大臣证实，因参加 2019 年香港民主抗议活动而受到的起诉不会阻止其他符合资格的申请人获得英国国家（海外）签证途径。英国议会大厦，威斯敏斯特，伦敦。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。英国人权联合委员会寻求澄清，因为担心因与 2019 年示威和骚乱有关的罪行而被定罪的具有 BN(O) 身份的人可能会被拒绝入境或留下来。周三，内政大臣沙巴纳·马哈茂德回复了一封信
content:
英国内政大臣证实，因参加 2019 年香港民主抗议活动而受到的起诉不会阻止其他符合资格的申请人获得英国国家（海外）签证途径。英国议会大厦，威斯敏斯特，伦敦。资料照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。英国人权联合委员会寻求澄清，因为担心因与 2019 年示威和骚乱有关的罪行而被定罪的具有 BN(O) 身份的人可能会被拒绝入境或留下来。周三，内政大臣沙巴纳·马哈茂德回复了委员会的一封信。她写道：“现在应该有一个假设，即确保与参加 2019 年抗议活动相关的定罪不会妨碍其他符合资格的个人从 BN(O) 路线中受益。因参加亲民主抗议活动而不符合标准 BN(O) 路线适用性要求的 BN(O) 路线申请人现在将自动被部长考虑在移民规则之外授予休假资格。”她补充说：“我感到自豪的是，英国已经为数千名香港人提供了安全港，政府将继续与香港人民站在一起。” 2019 年 12 月 8 日的抗议活动。照片：May James/HKFP。 2019 年 6 月，针对已被废除的引渡法案爆发了抗议活动。
在呼吁民主和对北京的侵犯感到愤怒的背景下，他们有时升级为对警察行为的暴力表达。示威者要求对警察行为进行独立调查，赦免被捕者，并停止将抗议活动定性为“骚乱”。  7月下旬，前民主党主席胡志伟抵达英国后在伦敦希思罗机场被拦截，在边境被拘留10小时后最初仅获得7天的移民保释。胡志伟在 2019 年的抗议活动中。照片：FTVV 截图。吴根据北京实施的国家安全法因阴谋颠覆国家而被定罪。他是被指控在 2020 年 7 月举行非官方民主立法会初选的 47 名民主党人之一。这位 63 岁的人被判入狱四年零五个月。英国当局后来批准他在该国居留六个月。已签发超过 230,000 份签证 人权联合委员会是一个议会小组，由来自下议院和上议院任命的 12 名成员组成。根据周三的新闻稿，人权联合委员会主席亚历克斯·索贝尔 (Alex Sobel) 表示：“BN(O) 路线的设立是专门为了确保英国能够成为那些因捍卫民主自由而受到不公正惩罚的人的庇护所。他们因参加抗议活动而被定罪，不应阻止人们参与这一计划。”
政府认识到这个问题并采取适当的行动来纠正它是正确的。”上周，英国表示，在英国的香港 BN(O) 签证持有者将不受一项将定居资格期限加倍至 10 年的提议的豁免。香港人的签证计划是在北京于 2020 年颁布香港国安法后推出的。据内政部称，截至今年 2 月，已有超过 23 万人获得了 BN(O) 签证，近 17 万人移居英国。北京于2020年6月将国家安全立法直接纳入香港小宪法

【原文 English Original】
Britain’s home secretary has confirmed that prosecutions for taking part in the 2019 pro-democracy protests in Hong Kong will not prevent otherwise eligible applicants from accessing the British National (Overseas) visa route. The UK Houses of Parliament, Westminster, London. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The UK’s Joint Committee on Human Rights had sought the clarification amid concerns that people with BN(O) status convicted of offences connected to the 2019 demonstrations and unrest could be denied entry or leave to remain. On Wednesday, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood responded to a letter from the committee. She wrote: “[T]here should now be a presumption in favour of ensuring that convictions connected to participation in the 2019 protests do not prevent otherwise eligible individuals from benefiting from the BN(O) route. BN(O) route applicants who do not meet the standard BN(O) route suitability requirements due to participation in the pro-democracy protests will now be automatically considered by Ministers for a grant of leave outside the Immigration Rules.” “I am proud that the UK has already provided a safe haven to thousands of Hong Kongers and the Government will continue to stand with the people of Hong Kong,” she added. A protest on December 8, 2019. Photo: May James/HKFP. Protests erupted in June 2019 over a since-axed extradition bill . They escalated into sometimes violent displays of dissent against police behaviour, amid calls for democracy and anger over Beijing’s encroachment. Demonstrators demanded an independent probe into police conduct, amnesty for those arrested and a halt to the characterisation of protests as “riots.”  In late July, ex-Democratic Party chair Wu Chi-wai was stopped at London’s Heathrow Airport upon arriving in the UK and initially granted only seven days of immigration bail following a 10-hour detention at the border. Wu Chi-wai at the 2019 protests. Photo: FTVV screenshot. Wu was convicted under the Beijing-imposed national security law for conspiracy to subvert the state. He was among 47 democrats accused of holding an unofficial pro-democracy legislative primary election in July 2020. The 63-year-old was jailed for four years and five months. UK authorities later granted him leave to remain in the country for six months. Over 230,000 visas issued The Joint Committee on Human Rights is a parliamentary group of 12 members appointed from both the House of Commons and the House of Lords. According to a Wednesday press release, Chair of the Joint Committee on Human Rights Alex Sobel said: “The BN(O) route was set up specifically to ensure that the UK could be a place of sanctuary to those who were unjustly punished for standing up for their democratic freedoms. Convictions they received for taking part in the protests should not preclude people from accessing this scheme. It is right that the Government has recognised this issue and taken the appropriate action to remedy it.” Last week, the UK said Hong Kong BN(O) visa holders in the UK would be exempt from a proposal to double the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years. The visa scheme for Hongkongers was introduced following the 2020 enactment of the Beijing-imposed security law in the city. As of February this year, over 230,000 people had been granted a BN(O) visa and almost 170,000 had moved to the UK, according to the Home Office. Beijing inserted national security legislation directly into Hong Kong’s mini-constitution in June 2020 following a year of pro-democracy protests and unrest. It criminalised subversion, secession, collusion with foreign forces and terrorist acts – broadly defined to include disruption to transport and other infrastructure. The move gave police sweeping new powers and led to hundreds of arrests amid new legal precedents , while dozens of civil society groups disappeared . The authorities say it restored stability and peace to the city, rejecting criticism from trade partners , the UN and NGOs .

title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: US media
zh_title: 美媒：英伟达准备罢免CEO黄仁勋
summary: 美国媒体周三报道称，英伟达董事会正准备罢免其联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋，因为该芯片巨头的首席执行官在被曝与一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染后，面临新的不忠指控。 Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2026 年 1 月 5 日在内华达州拉斯维加斯举行的年度消费电子展之前，在 CES 2026 的 Nvidia Live 上发表讲话。照片：Patrick T. Fallon/法新社。据《华尔街日报》援引知情人士的消息称，该科技公司董事会正准备最快于周三召开会议，以确定黄的未来。
content:
美国媒体周三报道称，英伟达董事会正准备罢免其联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋，因为该芯片巨头的首席执行官在被曝与一名被指控为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染后，面临新的不忠指控。 Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2026 年 1 月 5 日在内华达州拉斯维加斯举行的年度消费电子展之前，在 CES 2026 的 Nvidia Live 上发表讲话。照片：Patrick T. Fallon/法新社。据《华尔街日报》援引知情人士的话称，该科技公司董事会正准备最快于周三召开会议，以确定黄的未来。 《纽约时报》周三报道称，黄还与一名下属发生了第二次婚外情，称有视频证据显示这位 63 岁的高管与英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔 (Kimberly Powell) 关系密切。据《泰晤士报》报道，48 岁的鲍威尔一直是英伟达努力将芯片技术扩展到高等教育和医疗保健领域的公开代言人，他在加利福尼亚州圣何塞举行的一次会议上发表了讲话，旁观者“看到他们在酒店里充满感情”。在报道第二起事件之前，黄承认与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高级管理人员 Alice Huang 存在关系。 《华尔街日报》报道称，两人曾于2024年和2025年在台北被拍到在一起。
Nvidia 创始人、总裁兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2025 年 4 月 30 日在华盛顿特区举行的 2025 年 Hill & Valley 论坛上。照片：The Hill and Valley 论坛，来自 YouTube。据报道，美国情报部门去年春天散发了一份备忘录，指控黄爱丽是中国国家安全部的资产。这位英伟达首席执行官在周日给英伟达员工的一封信中承认与黄仁勋有关系——他与黄仁勋没有任何亲属关系——并写道：“我对我的妻子不忠。”同一天，英伟达董事会在一份声明中表示，他们“根据最近有关创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋成为外国情报工作目标的报道，启动了一项独立调查”。另请参阅：英伟达首席执行官事件再次推动美国对中国采取更强硬立场“我支持调查并将全力配合。我爱我们的国家和我们的公司，”黄在声明中写道。据《泰晤士报》报道，国会还要求他就他与爱丽丝黄的互动提供闭门简报。随着人工智能行业的蓬勃发展，英伟达的股价再创新高，黄仁勋在白宫活动中出现在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普身边，就在上个月，他接受了共和党领导人颁发的国家科学奖章。 2025 年 4 月 30 日星期三，在白宫十字厅举行的“投资美国”活动中，NVIDIA 首席执行官黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统的注视下发表讲话。
照片：白宫，来自 Flickr.Huang 是世界上最有影响力的科技领袖之一，其中包括埃隆·马斯克、杰夫·贝索斯和马克·扎克伯格，他们誓言要对人工智能进行自我监管，以应对可能的威胁，而特朗普拒绝了政府监管的呼吁，并驳回了该技术可能消灭人类的警告。英伟达股东对黄仁勋和这家人工智能芯片制造商提起集体诉讼，理由是他们未能向投资者披露有关双方关系的信息。自黄仁勋承认此事以来，英伟达股价近几天暴跌。 Nvidia 设计先进组件起源

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, US media reported Wednesday, as the chip giant’s chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. Photo: Patrick T. Fallon/AFP. The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The report of the second affair follows Huang’s acknowledgment of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. Nvidia founder, president and CEO Jensen Huang at the Hill & Valley Forum 2025 in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo: The Hill and Valley Forum, via YouTube. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Huang — to whom he bears no familial relation — in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday, writing: “I was unfaithful to my wife.” The same day Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement that they’d launched “an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” See also: Nvidia CEO affair revives push for tougher US line on China “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote in his statement. He has also been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, the Times reported. As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang delivers remarks as President Donald Trump looks on during an “Investing in America” event, Wednesday, April 30, 2025, in the Cross Hall of the White House. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders — including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg — who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Huang admitted to the affair. Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). Nvidia’s processors are mostly made by Taiwanese company TSMC, the world’s largest contract manufacturer of chips.

title: Nvidia board meets to decide CEO Huang’s future, source says
zh_title: 消息人士称，英伟达董事会召开会议决定首席执行官黄的未来
summary: 一位知情人士告诉路透社，英伟达董事会将于 11 月 11 日星期三召开会议，决定是否罢免首席执行官黄仁勋，因为这家全球主要的人工智能处理器供应商正在努力应对涉及其长期领导者的两起婚外情的报道。英伟达没有立即回应对董事会会议发表评论的请求。黄仁勋的潜在离职将导致这家芯片制造商出现领导真空，这家公司价值约 4 万亿美元，是他与人共同创立的，并在三十多年的时间里打造成为全球人工智能中心的人工智能芯片顶级供应商。
content:
一位知情人士告诉路透社，英伟达董事会将于 11 月 11 日星期三召开会议，决定是否罢免首席执行官黄仁勋，因为这家全球主要的人工智能处理器供应商正在努力应对涉及其长期领导者的两起婚外情的报道。英伟达没有立即回应对董事会会议发表评论的请求。黄仁勋的潜在离职将导致这家芯片制造商出现领导真空，这家由他共同创立并花费了三十多年时间打造的价值约 4 万亿美元的芯片制造商，将成为全球人工智能热潮和中美技术竞争中心的人工智能芯片顶级供应商。 63 岁的黄仁勋没有明显的继任者，拥有 Nvidia 约 3.6% 的股票。他还有数十名直接下属，这凸显了他对公司的严格控制。 D.A. 技术研究主管吉尔·卢里亚 (Gil Luria) 表示：“黄先生立即被免职可能对英伟达来说是一个挑战，因为它没有制定继任计划……如果黄先生违法或违反公司政策，董事会可能会在掌握证据后立即采取行动。”戴维森说。在《华尔街日报》首次报道英伟达准备罢免黄仁勋之后，该公司股价在盘后交易中下跌约 8%。包括周三的盘后抛售在内，自董事会宣布对英伟达与一名中国女商人的关系进行调查以来，英伟达本周的股价已损失约 6000 亿美元。
当天早些时候，《纽约时报》报道称，黄仁勋还与一名向他汇报的公司高管发生了婚外情。 《纽约时报》援引五名在该公司工作的人士称，这段关系的对象是英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔(Kimberly Powell)。当周三通过电话询问他与鲍威尔的关系时，黄先生说，“我认为你不应该直接和我说话。”据《纽约时报》报道，他随后挂断了电话。英伟达和鲍威尔没有立即回应置评请求。路透社无法立即核实该报道。领导层的不确定性 这些报道标志着一场争议的急剧升级，这场争议始于黄与爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 关系的曝光，美国情报部门称，爱丽丝·黄参与了向中国公司运送英伟达芯片的活动。美国股指期货下跌，纳斯达克期货下跌 1%。然而，竞争对手芯片制造商 AMD 和 Broadcom 的股价在盘后交易中分别上涨 4% 和 3%，一位分析师表示，这反映了这些芯片制造商将扩大市场份额的观点。投资者和分析师表示，虽然短期内对英伟达芯片的需求不太可能下降，但该公司支持的更广泛的公司可能会受到影响。新加坡 Vantage Point 资产管理公司首席投资官 Nick Ferres 表示：“Nvidia 也是循环融资的中心，为投资热潮提供资金。”
“他们正在为客户提供融资。在这些类型的繁荣或泡沫中，有时只需放慢速度即可将其转变为萧条阶段。”在周日发给员工的一份备忘录中，黄承认对妻子不忠，并承担“全部责任”，但没有透露这段关系的细节。同一天，英伟达董事会对黄仁勋是否成为外国情报机构的目标展开调查。该调查由独立董事和外部法律顾问监督。当时，董事会表示有信心

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia’s board is meeting on Wednesday, November 11, to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, as the world’s dominant supplier of AI processors grapples with reports of two extramarital affairs involving its longtime leader. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the board meeting. Huang’s potential departure would leave a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4-trillion chipmaker he co-founded and built over more than three decades to become the top supplier of AI chips at the center of the global artificial-intelligence boom and US-China technology rivalry. Huang, 63, has no obvious successor and owns about 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock. He also has dozens of direct reports, underscoring the tight control he maintains over the company. “Huang being removed immediately could be challenging for Nvidia since it does not have a succession plan in place … If Mr. Huang broke the law or violated company policies, the board is likely to act as soon as they have proof,” Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, said. The company’s shares slid about 8% in after-hours trading after the Wall Street Journal first reported that Nvidia was preparing to oust Huang. Including Wednesday’s after-hours selloff, Nvidia has lost about $600 billion in stock market value this week since the board announced its investigation into his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman. Earlier in the day, the New York Times reported that Huang had also had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him. The relationship was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, the New York Times said, citing five people who worked at the company. When reached by phone Wednesday and asked about his relationship with Ms. Powell, Mr. Huang said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly.” He then hung up, the New York Times reported. Nvidia and Powell did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Leadership uncertainty The reports mark a sharp escalation in a controversy that began with revelations about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , a woman US intelligence has said was involved in facilitating shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms. US stock futures sank, with Nasdaq futures down 1%. However, shares of rival chipmakers AMD and Broadcom rose 4% and 3%, respectively, in after-hours trading, which an analyst said reflected the view that those chip producers would pick up market share. Investors and analysts said while demand for Nvidia’s chips would be unlikely to drop in the near term, the broader universe of companies backed by the company might suffer. “Nvidia is also at the center of the circular financing which is providing capital to the investment boom,” said Nick Ferres, chief investment officer at Vantage Point Asset Management in Singapore. “They are financing their customers. In these types of booms or bubbles, sometimes all it takes is a slowdown to shift it into the bust phase.” In a memo to employees on Sunday, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and took “full responsibility,” but gave no details about the relationship. The same day, Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The probe is being overseen by independent directors with outside legal counsel. At the time, the board expressed confidence in Huang. US President Donald Trump has said he had not discussed the allegations with Huang but voiced support for the Nvidia chief, calling him “an honorable guy” who had “done an amazing job for our country.” Huang faces a potential congressional subpoena if he doesn’t respond to a request to provide a closed-door briefing about the allegations that he had a close relationship with the Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Separately, Axios reported on Wednesday, citing high-level sources, that US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stalled President Donald Trump’s crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia’s chips to China. Must Read Trump’s close ties to Nvidia’s Huang scrutinized after foreign intelligence concerns The White House and a spokesperson for Lutnick did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 with Curtis Priem and Chris Malachowsky. Its early hits were graphics chips for computer games, before its CUDA software opened the processors to general computing and, later, AI. – Rappler.com

title: Jensen Huang may be out at Nvidia: The rise and fall of a key figure in the AI boom
