中新社台北11月11日电 台湾主计总署周三表示，今年前9个月，台湾工业和服务业平均名义月工资增幅创26年来第二高水平。
DGBAS编制的数据显示，1月至9月平均每月固定工资达到新台币49,152元（1,496美元），同比增长2.93%，为26年来第二高增幅，仅落后于2025年的3%。
数据显示，经过通胀调整后，前九个月实际平均月工资同比上涨0.98%，为六年来第二高，仅次于2025年的1.21%。
根据 DGBAS 的数据，实际平均常规工资的增长表明工资增长继续超过通货膨胀。
1-9月，随着政府的物价稳定措施缓解了通胀压力，应对国际能源成本的飙升，台湾的消费者价格指数同比上涨1.94%。
过去9个月，平均工资（包括固定工资和加班费、奖金等非固定工资）为新台币609,498元，比去年同期增长4.59%。
DGBAS表示，同期，收入增长也超过了通货膨胀，实际平均收入同比增长2.60%，创2015年以来的新高，当时的增长率为3.56%。
由于平均工资很容易受到两个极端值的扭曲，国家统计局还公布了9月份的平均月工资中位数，达到新台币39,793元，比去年同期增长2.93%。
1-9月平均月固定工资中位数为新台币39,429元，同比增长3.04%，经通胀调整后，增幅仍达1.08%。
接受记者采访时，??国土统计局人口普查处副处长谭文玲表示，随着政府近年来提高最低工资，以及雇主似乎热衷于提高薪酬以留住人才，台湾工人的工资中位数在这9个月中与2020年同期相比增长了15.48%。
此外，1-9月当地员工平均常规工资增幅也较2020年同期增长17.51%。
统计局称，今年前9个月，台湾正常工资低于全国平均水平的雇员人数占总雇员人数的69.97%，低于1-6月期间录得的70.03%的高位。

Taiwan's Jan.-Sept. regular wage growth hits 2nd highest in 26 years: DGBAS
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 11 (CNA) The growth of average nominal monthly regular wages in Taiwan's industrial and service sectors in the first nine months of this year hit the second-highest level in 26 years, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS) said on Wednesday.
Data compiled by the DGBAS showed average monthly regular wages hit NT$49,152 (US$1,496) during January to September, up 2.93 percent from a year earlier, the second highest growth in 26 years, only trailing 3 percent recorded in 2025.
After inflationary adjustments, real average monthly wages during the nine-month period rose 0.98 percent from a year earlier, the second highest in six years only after the 1.21 percent in 2025, the data indicated.
The growth in real average regular wages showed wage growth continued to beat inflation, according to the DGBAS.
During the January-September period, Taiwan's consumer price index rose 1.94 percent from a year earlier as the government's price stabilization measures eased inflationary pressure, taking on a spike in international energy costs.
Over the nine months, average earnings, comprising regular wages and nonregular wages such as overtime pay and bonuses, stood at NT$609,498, up 4.59 percent from a year earlier.
During the same period, the earnings growth also beat inflation with real average earnings up 2.60 percent from a year earlier, a new high since 2015, when growth stood at 3.56 percent, the DGBAS said.
With average wages easily distorted by values at the two extremes, the DGBAS also announced the average median monthly wages which hit NT$39,793 in September, up 2.93 percent from a year earlier.
In the January-September period, average median monthly regular wages stood at NT$39,429, up 3.04 percent from a year earlier, and after inflationary adjustments, the growth still hit 1.08 percent.
Speaking with reporters,?? an Wen-ling (譚文玲), deputy director of the DGBAS Census Department, said that as the government raised the minimum wage in recent years and employers appeared keen to raise compensation to retain talent, median wage growth for Taiwanese workers hit 15.48 percent during the nine months, compared with the same period of 2020.
In addition, average regular wage growth for local employees during January-September also rose 17.51 percent from the same period of 2020.
In the first nine months of this year, the number of employees in Taiwan whose regular wage was below the national average accounted for 69.97 percent of the total workers, down from a high of 70.03 percent recorded during the January-June period, the DGBAS said.

中新社台北11月11日电 台湾数码事务部(MODA)周三表示，最近针对台湾10多家企业和在线平台的网络攻击中，近一半涉及人工智能(AI)，其中一些攻击流量似乎来自香港。
官员们在台北举行的新闻发布会上表示，这些攻击影响了超过 100 万条个人记录，包括姓名、电话号码、电子邮件地址和订单详细信息。
MODA网络安全管理局官员黄卓伦表示，初步调查显示，近一半的攻击与人工智能有关，其中一些涉及ARTEX，这是一种中国开发的自动化工具，用于测试系统或网站的安全漏洞。
周三，数字事务部网络安全管理局官员 Julius Huang 在台北举行的新闻发布会上介绍了与人工智能相关的网络攻击。中央通讯社照片2026年11月11日
黄说：“人工智能帮助黑客自动找到门并尝试钥匙。”他解释说，该技术允许攻击者更快、以更低的成本利用弱密码和未修补的软件等“安全漏洞”。
MODA 网络安全管理局事件通知和响应部门主任黄补充道，在审查的案件中，尚未确认信用卡或其他支付信息遭到泄露。
国家网络安全研究所所长龚化中表示，最新一波浪潮始于九月中旬左右，韩国报告了第一例病例。他说，截至 10 月 20 日，当局已发现台湾发生了多起袭击事件，而且袭击浪潮仍在持续。
国家网络安全研究所所长 Dennis Kung 周三在台北举行的新闻发布会上分享了对人工智能相关网络攻击的见解。中央通讯社照片2026年11月11日
Kung 说，一些攻击流量似乎来自香港，而其他攻击流量则通过不同国家的服务器进行路由。
他说：“如果他们来自台湾境内，我们肯定会抓到他们，但到目前为止我们看到的病例都来自海外。”
数码事务部长林宜敬警告说，追踪到香港的IP地址并不能确定黑客的实际位置。
林拒绝透露受影响企业的名称，理由是可能造成财务和声誉损失。
“对于上市公司来说，这可能会影响他们的股价，”林说。 “对于非上市公司来说，对个别案件发表评论可能会损害他们的声誉。”
披露近期违规行为的公司包括电子商务服务提供商 91APP（该公司表示多达 480 万消费者可能受到影响）和在线旅行社 ezTravel（该公司报告有超过 69 万会员受到影响）。
MODA 没有确认这两家公司是否包含在其统计中。
当被问及赔偿问题时，林表示，如果违规行为导致与欺诈相关的损失，公司可能会面临法律责任，但他没有提及消费者是否可以仅因个人数据泄露而寻求赔偿。

Nearly half of recent cyberattacks on Taiwan firms AI-linked: MODA

Digital Affairs Minister Lin Yi-jing (center) speaks at a news conference on AI-related cyberattacks in Taipei on Wednesday. CNA photo Nov. 11, 2026
Taipei, Nov. 11 (CNA) Nearly half of recent cyberattacks targeting more than 10 businesses and online platforms in Taiwan involved artificial intelligence (AI), with some attack traffic appearing to originate from Hong Kong, the Ministry of Digital Affairs (MODA) said on Wednesday.
The attacks affected more than 1 million personal records, including names, phone numbers, email addresses, and order details, officials told a news conference in Taipei.
Julius Huang (黃卓倫), an official at MODA's Administration for Cyber Security, said preliminary investigations linked nearly half the attacks to AI, with some involving ARTEX, a Chinese-developed automated tool used to test security weaknesses in systems or websites.
Julius Huang, an official at the Ministry of Digital Affairs' Administration for Cyber Security, gives a presentation on AI-related cyberattacks at a news conference in Taipei on Wednesday. CNA photo Nov. 11, 2026
"AI helps hackers automatically find doors and try keys," Huang said, explaining that the technology allows attackers to exploit "security vulnerabilities," such as weak passwords and unpatched software, quicker and at lower cost.
No breaches of credit card or other payment information have been confirmed in the cases reviewed, added Huang, director of the Incident Notification and Response Division at MODA's cybersecurity administration.
Dennis Kung (龔化中), president of the National Institute of Cyber Security, said the latest wave began around mid-September, with the first cases reported in South Korea. The authorities had identified several attacks in Taiwan by Oct. 20, and the wave was still ongoing, he said.
National Institute of Cyber Security President Dennis Kung shares insights into AI-related cyberattacks at a news conference in Taipei on Wednesday. CNA photo Nov. 11, 2026
Some attack traffic appeared to come from Hong Kong, while others were routed through servers in different countries, Kung said.
"If they came from within Taiwan, we would definitely catch them, but the cases we've seen so far have all come from overseas," he said.
Digital Affairs Minister Lin Yi-jing (林宜敬) cautioned that IP addresses traced to Hong Kong did not establish the hackers' actual locations.
Lin declined to name the affected businesses, citing potential financial and reputational damage.
"For publicly traded companies, it could affect their share prices," Lin said. "For non-listed companies, commenting on individual cases could damage their reputations."
Companies that have disclosed recent breaches include e-commerce service provider 91APP, which said up to 4.8 million consumers could have been affected, and online travel agency ezTravel, which reported more than 690,000 affected members.
MODA did not confirm whether either company was included in its tally.
Asked about compensation, Lin said companies could face legal liability if breaches led to fraud-related losses, but did not address whether consumers could seek compensation for the exposure of their personal data alone.
Meanwhile, Huang Ya-ping (黃雅萍), deputy director-general of the Administration for Digital Industries, said digital economy businesses were required to report personal data breaches to MODA within 72 hours of becoming aware of them.
The ministry also urged businesses to notify affected customers and take steps to contain breaches within 72 hours of discovering the breach, as well as submit improvement plans within one month.
Huang warned that scammers could use leaked order details to impersonate retailers and lure consumers into fake customer service accounts on the messaging app LINE under the pretext of canceling recurring payments.

台湾立法院首次使用人工智能阅读法案

周三，立法院社会福利与环境卫生委员会的议员们在台北听取 AI 宣读《痴呆症基本法》的 15 个版本拟议修正案。中央通讯社照片2026年11月11日
中新社台北11月11日电 立法院周三首次使用人工智能(AI)朗读立法提案。
立法院社会福利与环境卫生委员会的议员们同意使用人工智能阅读《痴呆症基本法》拟议修正案的 15 个版本，这是该法案审查开始前的标准程序。
委员会主席陈菁徽表示，人工智能最初以正常速度的 1.5 倍阅读 10 分钟，后来立法者表示他们没有困难，随后增加到正常速度的两倍，并在 70 分钟内完成阅读。
国民党立法委员陈表示，立法人员需要大约2小时11分钟来阅读全部15项提案。
她希望人工智能的首次使用将为立法机构更广泛采用人工智能铺平道路。
这个想法是在陈在2024年的一次全体会议上失去声音并使用人工智能生成的声音向卓荣泰总理提问后产生的。
陈说，立法院院长韩国瑜此后鼓励立法院探索人工智能的使用，并成立了一个工作组来研究其应用。
她说，在周三的会议之前，该委员会与立法机关信息技术部合作测试该应用程序并确保其准确性。

Taiwan's Legislature uses AI to read bills for 1st time

Lawmakers on the Legislature's Social Welfare and Environmental Hygiene Committee listen as AI reads out 15 versions of proposed amendments to the Dementia Basic Act in Taipei on Wednesday. CNA photo Nov. 11, 2026
Taipei, Nov. 11 (CNA) The Legislative Yuan used artificial intelligence (AI) to read proposed legislation aloud for the first time on Wednesday.
Lawmakers on the Legislature's Social Welfare and Environmental Hygiene Committee agreed to use AI to read 15 versions of proposed amendments to the Dementia Basic Act, a standard procedure before the bill's review began.
The AI initially read at 1.5 times its normal speed for 10 minutes before increasing to twice the normal speed after lawmakers said they had no difficulty keeping up, completing the reading in 70 minutes, committee chair Chen Ching-hui (陳菁徽) said.
Chen, a Kuomintang (KMT) lawmaker, said legislative staff would have needed about two hours and 11 minutes to read all 15 proposals.
She hoped the first use of AI would pave the way for its wider adoption in the Legislature.
The idea came after Chen once lost her voice and used an AI-generated version of her voice to question Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) during a plenary session in 2024.
Chen said Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜) has since encouraged the Legislature to explore AI use and established a task force to study its applications.
Before Wednesday's meeting, the committee worked with the Legislature's Information Technology Department to test the application and ensure its accuracy, she said.

content:
路透社星期三(11月11日)报道说，一所与中国人民解放军关系密切的中国高校10月份购入了英伟达(Nvidia)性能强大的H200先进芯片，这凸显了美国在限制中国获取先进技术方面存在漏洞。
路透社在这篇独家报道中披露，根据中国西北工业大学官网10月21日发布的一份采购记录，该校上个月购入了2枚H200芯片，总价为87.47万元人民币(约合12.3万美元)。
报道称，采购记录显示，这些芯片并非直接从英伟达购入，而是由该校管理学院通过一家位于陕西西安市的企业--陕西博算网络科技有限公司进行采购的。
美国之音记者在西北工业大学官网搜索，发现所有相关新闻页面已经消失了。
西北工业大学属于中国知名的“国防七校”(即工信部直属七所国防类重点高校)之一。作为中国顶尖的国防工业依托高校，该校长期深度参与中国人民解放军及各大国防工业集团在军事方面的科研工作。
西北工业大学从2001年起，便一直位列美国商务部的“实体清单”(Entity List)制裁名单上，该名单限制美国企业向其出口受管制的商品与技术。
H200是英伟达公司用于训练和运行先进超级智能(通常称人工智能或AI)系统的最强芯片之一，其出口受到美国的出口管制；特别对于像西北工业大学这种被列入制裁名单的机构，此类出口许可通常无法通过。
路透社的报道称，西北工业大学在位列美国出口管制“黑名单”时，仍可以完成此类采购，凸显了美国在限制中国获取先进技术方面存在漏洞。
今年1月，美国政府调整了英伟达H200的对华出口政策，开始允许符合条件的部分交易按个案申请许可；但该政策并未解除针对“实体清单”所列机构(如西北工业大学)的各项限制。
路透社还报道，采购记录显示，今年西北工业大学与多家中国本土科技供应商签订了五份算力租赁合同，从而得以使用H200芯片及英伟达其它高性能人工智能处理器。
近日，多个报道称英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)曾成为外国情报机构目标。这些报道指称黄仁勋与一位名叫黄乐(Alice Huang)的商界女性存在关联，而美国官员认定该女子为中国的情报人员。此消息在美国高科技业界及美国社会引发强烈关注。
黄仁勋一直在游说华盛顿放宽对华人工智能芯片销售限制。他曾主张，美国应继续向中国销售符合安全要求的产品，因为这既能维持美国的技术领先地位，也能确保中国客户持续依赖美国技术，而不会加快转向本土替代技术。
但是，黄仁勋的主张与一些美国国会议员的立场存在重大分歧。这些议员担心中国在获取英伟达最先进的人工智能芯片后，可能会加速人工智能系统开发与美国抗衡。
由于黄仁勋曾成为外国情报机构目标一事可能涉及美国国安问题，美国国会领导众议院外交委员会、常设情报委员会和中国问题特设委员会的共和党众议员布莱恩·马斯特(Brian Mast)、埃里克·“里克”·克劳福德(Eric “Rick” Crawford)和约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)要求黄仁勋在11月18日到国会，就此事进行说明。
在一封11月4日发给黄仁勋的信函中，三位议员写道：“至关重要的是，国会必须确定美国国家安全所面临的风险程度。”
现任众议院议长、共和党人麦克·约翰逊(Mike Johnson)星期二对美国媒体《政客》(Politico)表示，他支持把加强芯片出口管控的内容纳入年底的《国防授权法案》。
明年1月即将掌握参众两院控制权的民主党人也推动把限制对华出口芯片的立法条文纳入《国防授权法案》。
另外，11月5日，路透社援引知情人士的说法，大约有60万枚英伟达H200芯片，由于北京尚未批准进口，目前仍存放在香港，等待被运往中国。
美国之音就西工大购买英伟达先进芯片一事向美国商务部和国务院发出置评请求，截至发稿，尚未收到回应。

content:
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特在纽约美中关系全国委员会成立60周年晚宴上发表讲话。(2026年11月10日)
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)星期二(11月10日)在纽约表示，美国希望与中国建立“更加平衡”的经济关系，目标是“去风险，而非脱钩”。他指出，“贸易必须在不削弱任何一方主权的情况下推进双方的利益。”贝森特讲话之际，美中两国正积极准备两国元首即将于下星期在中国深圳举行的会晤。
贝森特是在美中关系全国委员会(National Committee on U.S.-China Relations)成立60周年晚宴上发表这番讲话。中国驻美大使谢锋也出席晚宴并致辞。
贝森特说，美国经济过度依赖外部供应，而中国经济则越来越依赖外部需求；美国应增加本土生产，中国则应扩大国内消费。贝森特称，这一主张并非对贸易伙伴抱有敌意，而是要以互惠原则减少双方经济失衡。
贝森特强调，“贸易必须在不削弱任何一方主权的情况下推进双方的利益。”而正是基于这种精神，“唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统才以这种态度对待我们与中国的关系。”贝森特说。
贝森特还提到，两国已设立贸易委员会和投资委员会，作为讨论具体经贸问题的平台。他说，贸易委员会将研究对双方各300亿美元非敏感商品给予更有利的关税待遇，并成立农业贸易工作组；中国此前也承诺在未来两年采购至少2500万吨美国大豆和1000万吨美国煤炭。投资委员会则将讨论美国企业进入中国市场，以及提高中国企业在美国经营的可预期性。
在超级智能(通常称人工智能或AI)方面，贝森特说，美方已与中方启动超级智能对话，旨在防范共同风险、避免误判。他还表示，两国不应对在此问题上的分歧抱有幻想
同场发言的中国驻美大使谢锋表示，中美应找到大国正确相处之道，尊重彼此的底线和红线，在公平原则下竞争，并坚持互惠合作。他说，中美合作有利于双方，对抗则会造成损失。谢锋此前也曾将台湾、民主与人权、中国的发展道路和制度，以及发展权列为中方所说的“四条红线”。
贝森特将在下星期前往中国，参加特朗普总统今年第三次与习近平的会晤。美中两国元首预计在11月18日至19日深圳举行的APEC领导人会议期间会晤。
双方尚未公布正式议程，从近期官员表态和贸易磋商看，谈判重点可能包括延长或巩固贸易休战。目前的贸易休战延至2027年1月10日。双方可能讨论如何避免期限届满后关税和反制措施再度升级，或为更广泛的贸易协议设定谈判方向。
此外，美国可能继续敦促北京落实包括农产品、稀土及其他关键矿产在内的采购承诺。贝森特此前提到，中国承诺未来两年采购至少2500万吨美国大豆和1000万吨美国煤炭。与此同时，美国希望中国加快稀土及关键矿产出口许可、改善供应；北京则关注美国针对中国的贸易限制。

content:
在中国广东省深圳市，可见即将举行的2026年中国亚太经济合作组织(APEC)峰会的标识。(2026年11月3日)
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)与中国国家主席习近平正准备下星期在深圳会晤。这是特朗普总统所领导的共和党在美国中期选举失利后首次与习近平会晤。美国中期选举会对此次会晤产生什么样的影响？美中在推动落实经贸承诺和超级智能(通常被称为人工智能或AI)风险管控方面，又将有何种进展？
美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特(Scott Bessent)星期二(11月10日)表示，他将陪同特朗普前往深圳，两国领导人随后还将在迈阿密再次会面。深圳会晤将是两人今年第三次会面，此前特朗普5月访问北京，习近平9月访问华盛顿。
这次会晤将在11月18日至19日举行的亚太经济合作组织(APEC)领导人会议期间进行，这正值共和党刚刚在美国中期选举中失利，而华盛顿也在敦促北京兑现采购美国农产品以及稀土和其他关键矿产供应方面的承诺。
不过，分析人士提醒，领导人频繁接触并不意味着双方即将取得重大突破。华盛顿智库战略与国际研究中心(CSIS)的专家在11月9日的一场简报会上表示，对深圳会晤成果的预期有限，更具实质性的成果可能留待12月在迈阿密举行的二十国集团(G20)峰会。
贝森特在为美中关系全国委员会11月10日纽约活动准备的讲话中，介绍了美中围绕特朗普政府所称的“超级智能”开展双边对话的进展。
他说，双方计划交流先进模型发布前的评估与测试做法，确保人类保有控制权，并建立直接沟通渠道，通报涉及相关模型的严重事件。他同时提醒，两国的利益与应对挑战的方式仍会存在差异。
这项工作承接了两国领导人9月同意建立技术对话与事件沟通渠道的安排。中方当时发布的会晤成果也表示，下一轮人工智能对话将在11月举行。
贝森特的讲话进一步说明了拟议合作的内容，但并未明确事件沟通渠道是否已经投入运作。
深圳会晤的一个具体观察点，是双方能否说明这些安排将如何运行，把合作意向转化为可执行的机制。
中国本星期采取措施，为后续磋商保留空间。中方11月9日宣布，自11月10日起，继续暂停对美国商品加征的24%关税，为期两个月，同时保留10%的加征关税。北京表示，此举是为了落实两国领导人9月在华盛顿会晤达成的共识。
中国商务部还宣布，继续暂停针对16家美国实体的出口管制管控名单措施，以及针对11家美国实体的不可靠实体清单措施。相关交易仍须遵守适用的许可与审核要求。
与此同时，华盛顿要求北京以具体行动证明此前承诺正在落实。
贝森特与美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)11月6日同中国国务院副总理何立峰举行视频通话，讨论两国经贸关系。美国贸易代表办公室的通报说，格里尔强调，中方应采取具体行动，全面履行此前承诺，特别是在农产品采购、稀土及其他关键矿产方面。
北京则将扩大采购与降低关税联系起来。中国商务部发言人黄玲11月5日表示，中方一直对扩大自美采购农产品持开放态度，但前提是双方达成的“300亿对300亿”对等降税安排落地。
贝森特星期二再次提及，双方正推动为各自从对方进口的300亿美元非敏感商品提供更优惠的关税待遇，并通过双边投资机制讨论相关问题。他将美国的目标概括为“去风险，而非脱钩”。
战略与国际研究中心(CSIS)中国商业与经济研究项目副主任伊拉里娅·马佐科(Ilaria Mazzocco)在简报会上表示，对等降税安排的落实与双边贸易理事会的工作，是值得关注的进展指标。她说，半导体出口限制仍可能成为新的摩擦来源。
这次亚洲之行也为特朗普提供了一个机会，在中期选举之后向外界展示他在外交事务上的主导地位。
美国前驻马来西亚大使、现任战略与国际研究中心费里曼中国研究讲座主任埃德加·卡根(Edgard Kagan)在简报会上表示，总统在经历不利的中期选举后出访，可以向国内外传递自己仍掌握外交政策主导权的信息。
史汀生中心(Stimson Center)中国项目主任孙韵在接受美国之音中文采访时表示，美国国会的变化不一定会促使北京调整对特朗普政府的政策。
“我并不认为说中方对美国的判断以及政策会发生很重大的变化。”她说。
孙韵提醒，不应将国会控制权的变化等同于特朗普对华政策的根本转向。
她说，国会可以通过听证、调查以及对总统决策的监督，增加政府执行政策的难度。但特朗普本人的偏好与白宫决策仍将影响美中关系的走向。
“对于北京来说，北京肯定会面临更多的不确定性，但是这个不确定性也不是无限的。”她说。
孙韵表示，台湾只是国会可能向白宫施压的议题之一。双边贸易、中国在美国的投资，以及涉及新疆、西藏和香港的人权问题，也可能成为争议焦点。
在她看来，对北京而言，继续寻求与特朗普政府合作，可能比期待新一届国会采取更友善的对华立场更为现实。
特朗普、习近平与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)可能举行的三方会晤，也可能扩大深圳期间的讨论范围，不过相关安排尚未最终确定。
《华尔街日报》援引熟悉筹备工作的知情人士报道，北京希望三方会晤严格按照预先安排进行，由领导人分别宣读准备好的声明，尽量减少即席讨论；特朗普政府则主张采用更灵活的形式，让三位领导人有更多直接交流。
报道还援引一名中国官员的话说，北京愿意主办会晤，但要求事先商定议程与预期成果；如果准备不足，中方更倾向于分别举行双边会晤。双方在会晤形式与议程上的分歧，为三方会晤能否举行增添了不确定性。
中国外交部11月10日表示，中方就中俄美元首会晤同相关方保持沟通，但没有提供更多细节。特朗普星期天表示，可能的会谈将涉及无核化以及结束伊朗战争的努力。
孙韵对北京能否在伊朗问题上作出重大让步持怀疑态度。她认为，中国不太可能大幅减少进口伊朗原油，这限制了北京为特朗普提供足以带来显著政治收益的帮助的空间。
她还表示，特朗普政府接下来如何调整伊朗政策仍不清晰，因此，现在判断伊朗冲突将如何影响华盛顿对北京的政策，为时尚早。
尽管存在这些不确定因素，孙韵认为，与其推测特朗普会在选举后重新调整对华政策，不如观察他在第二任期已经展现出的偏好。
“就他本人的意愿，跟他目前所第二任期所表现出来的偏好来看，我并不认为现在特朗普对华政策的大方向会发生很大变化。”她说。

Lithium prices are getting harder to predict after a rollercoaster ride this year, according to Ganfeng Lithium Group, one of China’s top producers of the battery metal.
Market swings have become more extreme and price cycles have gotten shorter, president assistant Roy Zhang said at a conference in Shanghai on Wednesday.
“We have seen an entire price cycle just from the beginning of this year, which is not quite common,” said Zhang. “I don’t think anyone has an obvious view about where the price will be in the next 6 to 12 months.”
Lithium remains a nascent, fast-growing market, which makes it challenging to forecast as supply, demand and trading activity all expand at a breakneck pace. On the Guangzhou Futures Exchange where the metal is traded, sentiment rather than market fundamentals often dominates activity.
The market has been engulfed by heightened volatility this year due to uncertainty over supply from major production hubs, and changes in the structure of demand. In addition to electric vehicles, large batteries for energy storage systems have emerged as a meaningful pillar of consumption and are playing a bigger role in assessing the industry’s outlook.
Spot prices of lithium carbonate in China are 23% lower this year at 91 500 yuan ($13 700) a ton, after slumping in recent weeks on growing concerns over the demand outlook. They had rallied to over 200 000 yuan in May.
Zhang said lithium demand is growing at 40% this year and supply is catching up quickly, which is “quite phenomenal.” But the market’s balance is delicate.
“Even a small disruption in the supply chain will change the market very fast,” he said. “Just one substantial failure of a mine operation could very quickly shift the market into a shortage.”

2026年11月11日，欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩在土耳其安塔利亚举行的联合国气候变化大会（COP31）期间，和巴西总统卢拉互致问候图像来源: Murad Sezer/REUTERS
（德国之声中文网）第31届联合国气候变化大会（COP31）周三（11月11日）在土耳其安塔利亚（Antalya）进入领导人“高级别会议”阶段，数十位领导人将在周三和周四发言。但不少重量级人物缺席，英国首相伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）是七国集团（G7）中唯一计划发言的领导人。大会期间发布的一项国际排名显示，世界上大多数主要经济体在应对气候变化方面表现不佳。
据法新社报道，欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩会到场，但法国总统马克龙、德国总理默茨和意大利总理梅洛尼都不出席，加拿大总理卡尼（Mark Carney）和日本首相高市早苗也不在最新名单上。法国政府称，11月11日是第一次世界大战停战纪念日，马克龙周四还要出席在爱尔兰举行的欧盟峰会。
2026年11月11日，联合国气候变化框架公约（UNFCCC）执行秘书西蒙·斯蒂尔、土耳其总统埃尔多安、欧盟委员会主席冯德莱恩和联合国秘书长古特雷斯与其他各国领导人，在土耳其安塔利亚举行的联合国气候变化大会（COP31）期间合影。图像来源: Murad Sezer/REUTERS
美国总统特朗普让美国退出了《巴黎协定》，再次当选后一直没有派官员参加气候谈判，这次也没有出席。中国国家主席习近平由国家副主席韩正代表出席。欧洲气候行动网络主任马丁内利（Chiara Martinelli）说：“我担心，欧盟最大经济体的领导人都不露面，冯德莱恩会在台上很孤单。”欧盟气候事务专员胡克斯特拉（Wopke Hoekstra）也承认，外界对这届大会的“期望不一定很高”。
出席的领导人包括土耳其总统埃尔多安、巴西总统卢拉和伊朗总统佩泽希齐扬（Masoud Pezeshkian）。卢拉上个月击败弗拉维奥·博索纳罗（Flavio Bolsonaro）赢得连任，令气候活动人士大大松了一口气。东道主土耳其正在推动一项自愿倡议，目标是到2035年把电力在全球能源消费中的占比提高到35%；欧盟则强调，电气化必须是“清洁”的。
据德新社报道，德国观察（Germanwatch）和新气候研究所（NewClimate Institute）发布的最新气候变化绩效指数（CCPI）显示，二十国集团（G20）大多数国家进展不足，这些国家的二氧化碳排放量占全球80%以上。英国是唯一获得高评级的二十国集团成员，排名第七。COP31的两个共同主持国土耳其和澳大利亚都落入最低档。
瑞典气候活动人士格蕾塔·通贝里自2021年以来首次出席联合国气候变化大会。她在第31届大会（COP31）上表示，峰会讨论和作出的决定可能关系到无数人的生死，但她认为，历届气候大会都未能阻止气候灾难。图像来源: Murad Sezer/REUTERS
由于没有国家被认为足以实现1.5摄氏度的温控目标，前三名再次空缺，丹麦、立陶宛和卢森堡分列第四至第六位。
全球最大的温室气体排放国中国，尽管在可再生能源发展趋势上处于领先地位，排名仍接近末尾。
德国下滑三位，排在第25位，这是它连续第三年下滑，其国家气候政策得分尤其低。

北京香山论坛多国代表对军用人工智能的潜在风险深表担忧。在美中两国准备举行高层会晤之际，武器自主化正急剧压缩决策时间，大国在此类技术管控上的分歧再度引发广泛讨论。
周一，中共为前总书记江泽民举行百岁冥诞纪念大会。周二，前总理朱镕基的遗体在八宝山公墓火化，天安门等地降半旗致哀。江泽民与朱镕基留给习近平怎样的遗产？习近平能否借助已经逝去的时代安抚当下的民心，进一步巩固自己的权力？
在欧盟释放信号，表示愿意让加拿大以“准成员”身份成为其特殊伙伴后，美国总统特朗普对此发出嘲讽，并表示，这一设想属于“敌对行为”。

英伟达正在调查创始人黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国特工的关系
2026 年 11 月 11 日星期三 - 10:30 世界标准时间
该公司周日宣布，“鉴于最近有报道称创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋已成为外国情报机构的目标”，将开始调查
英伟达董事会已对创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋展开独立调查，原因是黄仁勋与一名华裔女商人有婚外情，美国情报部门将这名女商人与北京的间谍活动联系起来。唐纳德·特朗普总统周一表示，联邦调查局正在调查此案。没有人被指控。
该公司周日宣布，“鉴于最近有报道称创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋已成为外国情报工作的目标”，它正在开始调查。黄承认与新加坡人工智能基础设施公司 Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 的关系，尽管与她同姓，但与黄没有任何关系。据雅虎财经报道，他在给员工的备忘录中写道：“我深感抱歉。”英伟达在一份声明中表示，“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密已被泄露”。
据《纽约时报》报道，一份由国务卿马可·卢比奥监督的机密情报报告将爱丽丝·黄与中国国家安全部联系起来，并得出结论称，她寻求有关先进芯片的信息并影响其在中国的大规模分销。据美国新闻报道，她的下落不明。 NBC新闻援引消息人士的话说，司法部正在对Megaspeed进行刑事调查，该公司涉嫌向中国运送受到出口限制的Nvidia芯片；商务部已对该公司展开调查。立法者呼吁举行国会听证会。
特朗普表示，他已与黄进行过交谈，黄告诉他，他不知道该女子是间谍。 “我们会调查此事。我知道联邦调查局正在调查，我认为他会没事的，”他在白宫表示，他对这些指控感到“惊讶”。
该案影响的是人工智能行业最重要的公司。根据 Silicon Analyst 的一项研究，Nvidia 控制着 80% 到 90% 的人工智能加速器市场，并采用台湾台积电 (TSMC) 生产的加州芯片进行设计。 63岁的黄出生于台湾，在俄勒冈州长大。美国限制英伟达最先进的芯片向中国销售，黄仁勋今年游说特朗普放松这些控制；据《国家报》报道，华盛顿后来允许向中国公司出售一系列H20芯片，以换取25%的收入。
周二，美国中期选举后主要科技股大幅下跌，英伟达股价周二再次承压。

Nvidia investigates founder Jensen Huang over his relationship with an alleged Chinese agent
Wednesday, November 11th 2026 - 10:30 UTC
The company announced on Sunday that it was starting the investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”
Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into founder and chief executive Jensen Huang after it emerged that he had an extramarital relationship with a businesswoman of Chinese origin whom US intelligence services link to Beijing’s espionage. President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI is investigating the case. No one has been charged.
The company announced on Sunday that it was starting the investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. Huang acknowledged the relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based AI infrastructure company Megaspeed, to whom he is not related despite sharing a surname. “I am deeply sorry,” he wrote in a memo to employees, according to Yahoo Finance. Nvidia said in a statement that it has no “reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia’s secrets have been compromised”.
According to The New York Times, a classified intelligence report, overseen by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, linked Alice Huang to China’s Ministry of State Security and concluded that she sought information on advanced chips and to influence their large-scale distribution in China. Her whereabouts are unknown, according to U.S. News. A source cited by NBC News also said the Justice Department is conducting a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, which is suspected of shipping export-restricted Nvidia chips to China; the Commerce Department already had an inquiry open into the company. Lawmakers have called for a congressional hearing.
Trump, who said he had spoken with Huang, said Huang told him he did not know the woman was a spy. “We’ll look into it. I know the FBI is investigating, and I think he’ll come out fine,” he said at the White House, where he said he was “amazed” by the allegations.
The case affects the most important company in the artificial intelligence industry. Nvidia controls between 80% and 90% of the AI accelerator market, according to a Silicon Analyst study, and designs in California chips that Taiwan’s TSMC manufactures. Huang, 63, was born in Taiwan and raised in Oregon. The United States restricts sales of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China, and Huang lobbied Trump this year to ease those controls; according to El País, Washington later allowed a series of H20 chips to be sold to Chinese companies in exchange for 25% of the revenue.
Nvidia shares came under renewed pressure on Tuesday, in a week when major tech stocks fell sharply after the US midterm elections.

中国的 Nvidia 蜜罐并不令人意外。黄仁勋无论如何都爱上了它|连线
在反情报简报会上，政府工作人员、军官和情报人员都被灌输了这样一句话：“如果她是 10 分，而你是 5 分，那么她就是间谍！”或者，正如美国陆军反情报司令部在情人节发布的那样：“不需要数学家就能算出‘10 + 5 = 美人计’。”这个非常漂亮的女人突然对你平凡的存在感兴趣，可能别有用心，这就是信息。
黄仁勋的生活肯定不是典型的——他是一位亿万富翁，是 Nvidia 虚张声势的首席执行官，Nvidia 是 21 世纪最热门、最具地缘政治影响力的公司之一。他当然意识到自己有可能与情报人员发生冲突。事实上，很难想象世界上有多少公司会成为外国情报机构更优先的目标。
所有这些都使得本周震动股市的消息更加令人惊讶。黄是如何卷入一场将不忠、国际间谍活动、特朗普政府和价值数万亿美元的人工智能行业的经济庞然大物混合在一起的间谍丑闻的？
故事从万圣节前夕开始，《纽约时报》刊登了一篇六行文章，报道称黄是中国间谍阴谋的目标。据称，从 2024 年到 2025 年期间开始，黄与 Alice Huang（无亲属关系）有染，后者曾是新加坡一家名为 Megaspeed 的云提供商的高管。美国情报机构警告美国高级官员，他们认为她是中国情报人员。到目前为止，已经启动调查的英伟达董事会表示，“没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密遭到泄露”，但这远不是唯一的担忧。
正如人们所预料的那样，中国否认有任何以黄仁勋为中心的邪恶阴谋。中国外交部发言人周一表示，“所谓中国间谍的说法完全是无端猜测，纯属污蔑抹黑”。
但据《纽约时报》和《金融时报》报道，美国情报官员还声称，黄乐（又名黄乐）正在向中国国家安全部情报机构汇报工作。周一，Megaspeed 在 LinkedIn 上表示，美国当局“没有发现任何涉及非法转让芯片或任何非法活动的证据”。 （到目前为止，没有任何迹象表明曾任中国国家记者的黄爱丽是中国情报部门的雇员或“官员”；她被认为是一个“资产”，一个为情报机构提供帮助的局外人，有时是为了报酬，有时不是。）
然而，中国已将经济间谍活动提升为其经济和军事发展的核心支柱，窃取从美国战斗机到太阳能电池板和商业油漆配方等各种设计。 “蜜罐”或“美人陷阱”——布置一个诱人的特工来引诱关键目标或与关键目标建立关系——是情报部门最臭名昭著、最行之有效的策略之一。至少从 2011 年起，法国官员就对中国蜜罐发出了特别警告，当时情报报告援引了一名被中国间谍行动引诱并勒索的药物研究人员的消息。

【原文 English Original】
China’s Nvidia Honeypot Isn’t Surprising. Jensen Huang Fell for It Anyway | WIRED
There’s a specific mantra drilled into government workers, military officers, and intelligence personnel during counterintelligence briefings: “If she’s a 10 and you’re a 5, she’s a spy!” Or, as the US Army’s Counterintelligence Command posted on Valentine’s Day: “It doesn’t take a mathematician to figure out ‘10 + 5 = honeytrap.’” The very beautiful woman who is suddenly interested in your very ordinary existence probably has ulterior motives, is the message.
Jensen Huang surely doesn’t live a typical life—he’s a centibillionaire, the swashbuckling CEO of Nvidia, one of the hottest and most geopolitically consequential companies of the 21st century. Surely he’s aware of the possibility that he’d cross paths with intelligence assets. In fact, it’s hard to think of many companies in the world that would be a higher priority target for foreign intelligence agencies.
All of that makes the stock-shaking news this week all the more surprising. How did Huang get embroiled in a spy scandal that mixes infidelity, international espionage, the Trump administration, and the economic behemoth of the multitrillion-dollar AI industry?
The story kicked off just before Halloween, with a six-byline story in The New York Times reporting that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Starting somewhere between 2024 and 2025, Huang allegedly had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a one-time executive at a Singapore-based cloud provider known as Megaspeed. US intelligence agencies warned top US officials that they believed she was a Chinese intelligence asset. So far, Nvidia’s board, which has launched its own investigation, says it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised,” but that’s far from the only concern.
As one would expect, China has denied any nefarious plot centered on Jensen Huang. A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson on Monday said, “The narrative about so-called Chinese spies is entirely based on groundless speculation—it’s nothing more than slander and smearing.”
But according to reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times, US intelligence officials also claim that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was reporting to China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency. On Monday, Megaspeed said on LinkedIn that US authorities found “no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities." (There’s no indication so far that Alice Huang, a one-time Chinese state journalist, is an employee or “officer” of Chinese intelligence; she’s believed to be an “asset,” an outsider who aids an intelligence agency, sometimes for pay, sometimes not.)
China, though, has elevated economic espionage to a core pillar of its economic and military development, stealing the designs for everything from US fighter jets to solar panels and commercial paint recipes. “Honeypots” or “honey traps”—positioning an alluring operative to seduce or develop a relationship with a key target—are one of intelligence’s most infamous and well-established strategies. French officials have warned specifically about Chinese honeypots since at least 2011, when intelligence reports cited a pharmaceutical researcher who was seduced and then blackmailed by a Chinese spy operation.
Over the past quarter of a century, as Silicon Valley emerged as a center of political and economic power, it has become a key focus of Chinese intelligence. In one plot, a Chinese national named Fang Fang spent years trying to cozy up to Bay Area politicians, including then US Representative Eric Swalwell. (While intelligence officials at the time reportedly believed Fang to be an operative, law enforcement officials never brought any charges against her). When traveling to China, US business executives have become accustomed to leaving their regular phones and computers at home and using burner devices to prevent the installation of spyware or malware (as I did, when I traveled to China for WIRED in 2019 to report on Huawei). In 2012, when Leon Panetta was making his first trip to China as defense secretary, he and his team were advised to bathe and shower in the dark in the event his hotel room was bugged. Last year, the threat of honeypots prompted the US government to explicitly ban personnel working in China and Hong Kong from engaging in romantic or sexual relationships with Chinese citizens. More recently, US officials joined with allies to warn about China’s increasingly sophisticated “LinkedIn espionage”: using the business-focused social networking site to recruit and build relationships with unwitting executives.
Alice Huang’s Megaspeed, for its part, is a major Pacific region player in cloud services focused on the advanced computer chips that are the heart of Nvidia’s business. The Biden administration had sharply limited the export of cutting-edge chips globally to slow China’s development of AI, but Jensen Huang has successfully lobbied the Trump administration to loosen those restrictions.
Speaking at a press conference on Monday, Donald Trump denied having prior knowledge of Alice Huang’s potential espionage. “I didn’t hear about it then, but a lot of people have heard about it, and Jensen totally denies that,” Trump said. “I asked him that question: ‘Did you have any idea that she was a spy?’ He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’” On Tuesday, the Times reported that Marco Rubio had briefed Trump in May, right before Jensen Huang joined the president on Air Force One for a trip to China.
The veracity of Trump's claims will surely be investigated, especially in the context of the famous Watergate maxim: “What did the president know and when did he know it?” Nvidia’s CEO has been publicly linked to the Megaspeed executive since at least 2024 and Alice’s husband, Kang Weigh, has reportedly known Jensen since the 2010s. WIRED’s Lauren Goode reported on Monday that Jensen Huang, starting in 2025, hired Risa Heller’s crisis communications firm, which is well-versed in handling public sex scandals. This spring, secretary of state Marco Rubio evidently helped craft a classified memo inside the administration warning officials about Jensen Huang’s potentially compromising relationship.
Jensen Huang—who has developed an important reputation as AI’s number one cheerleader at the frontier of AI labs—is now stuck in an awkward situation. Is he an idiot, unaware that his paramour might have been a foreign intelligence asset? Merely reckless with his own reputation, fiduciary responsibility to Nvidia, and the technological security of the United States? Or a witting accomplice to undermining US national security?
Regardless of the truth, Nvidia loses. Shareholders have ridden a roller-coaster that has seen Nvidia’s stock rise by about 600 percent over the past five years, becoming the world’s second-most valuable company. In the past month, the stock has plummeted by a quarter. The disaster for Nvidia is just beginning, it seems, as lawsuits loom, including by its own shareholders.
Similarly, the Trump administration is likely to face real questions from the newly Democratic congress: When were the president and other top officials briefed about this intelligence threat? What communication, if any, did they make to Nvidia and to whom? Should more have been done by US intelligence to block Alice Huang from having access to Nvidia and its CEO?
The fact that Megaspeed is a major customer of Nvidia makes everything more complicated. Indeed, reports have circulated for at least a year that the US was concerned that Megaspeed was diverting chips to Chinese intelligence agencies, an allegation that could have massive consequences for the global AI race. Bloomberg this week reported that Megaspeed's subsidiaries have purchased billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips and that an audit requested by the US government last year found that Megaspeed couldn’t initially account for some 50,000 chips it had purchased.
Meanwhile, Nvidia’s Huang and President Trump developed a uniquely close professional relationship. They’ve met multiple times as Huang has pushed to loosen Biden-era export controls, which Trump has repeatedly relaxed; Huang has donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom project; while en route to Beijing earlier this year with a delegation of tech leaders, including Elon Musk and Tim Cook, Trump’s Air Force One actually made a special stop in Alaska to pick up Huang; Huang also attended a White House state dinner for Chinese president Xi Jinping and Trump, who in turn, awarded him a National Medal of Science earlier this fall.
The implication that Trump knew and did nothing for a year would make this one of the greatest counterintelligence failures of the past decade. There will be consequences: Across history, many have gone to prison for honeypot scandals; a former adviser was arrested just last year in a similar plot; though he was acquitted of committing economic espionage, he was convicted for making false statements to investigators.
Even in normal circumstances, corporate America’s tolerance of CEO misbehavior has shrunken dramatically. In recent years, CEOs at companies as varied as Nestlé, Kohl’s, BP, NBCUniversal, and the railroad Norfolk Southern have all resigned or been forced out after inappropriate relationships that violated company standards.
If Nvidia were any other company and Jensen Huang any other CEO, the facts of the scandal currently known would be enough to topple some heads. But Trump is still president, and November is only a third over. It’s not even clear that this will rank as the biggest scandal of the month—but it should.

summary: 拉里·库德洛 (Larry Kudlow) 呼吁英伟达 (Nvidia) 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 在中国间谍丑闻中辞职福克斯商业频道 (Fox Business) 主持人、前白宫经济顾问拉里·库德洛 (Larry Kudlow) 周二呼吁英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 辞职，他认为，涉及涉嫌中国间谍的指控以及日益严重的国家安全担忧使他无法继续领导这家人工智能芯片制造商。库德洛表示，在英伟达董事会和联邦当局调查黄先生与一名涉嫌为中国情报机构工作的女性的关系期间，黄先生应该主动辞职。
content:
拉里·库德洛呼吁英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋因中国间谍丑闻辞职
福克斯商业频道主持人、前白宫经济顾问拉里·库德洛周二呼吁英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋辞职，称涉及涉嫌中国间谍的指控以及日益严重的国家安全担忧使他无法继续领导这家人工智能芯片制造商。
库德洛表示，在英伟达董事会和联邦当局调查他与一名涉嫌为中国情报机构工作的女性的关系，以及有关可能向中国走私美国先进半导体的问题时，黄仁勋应该主动辞职。
库德洛在对库德洛的开场评论中表示，“至少黄先生应该运用一些常识，辞去英伟达的职务，包括首席执行官。”
黄周日承认，他与英伟达主要客户新加坡 Megaspeed 公司前高管 Alice Huang 有染。据报道，美国情报官员认为她代表中国国家安全部工作。
英伟达董事会周日宣布，已对其首席执行官成为外国情报机构攻击目标的报道展开独立调查。调查将由独立董事和外部顾问监督。
该委员会表示，没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密信息已被泄露。它还表达了对黄的领导能力的信心，并表示他正在配合调查。
唐纳德·特朗普总统周一表示，联邦调查局正在调查此事。
库德洛还指出，有报道称，国务卿马可·卢比奥监督了一份机密情报备忘录的准备工作，警告高级政府官员黄与涉嫌中国情报人员的关系。
《纽约时报》周二报道称，卢比奥在总统五月份访华期间亲自向特朗普通报了这些情报。
这场争议还引发了对 Megaspeed 的质疑，该公司因涉嫌先进的 Nvidia 芯片被非法转移到中国而受到调查。库德洛将芯片走私指控视为黄在调查进行期间放弃领导职务的另一个原因。
除了国家安全问题之外，库德洛警告说，这一丑闻还可能削弱公众对快速扩张的人工智能行业的信心。
库德洛表示：“黄先生最终会给整个人工智能革命带来非常坏的名声。”他指出，两党对数据中心的反对日益强烈，以及公众对人工智能的担忧。
库德洛承认，黄仁勋此前曾是该技术的有效倡导者，但他表示，此次曝光改变了这一评估。
“黄先生一直是人工智能革命的好代言人，但随着这些蜜罐/国家安全的曝光，他不再是人工智能革命的好代言人，”库德洛说。
他还警告说，民主党在参众两院取得多数席位可能会让黄受到国会的严格审查。
这场争议已经引起了国会山的关注。众议院三个委员会的共和党主席要求黄仁勋出席闭门简报会，介绍英伟达的安全程序及其意图

【原文 English Original】
Larry Kudlow Calls on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to Resign Amid Chinese Espionage Scandal
Fox Business host and former White House economic adviser Larry Kudlow called on Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to resign Tuesday, arguing that allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy and mounting national security concerns have made his continued leadership of the artificial intelligence chipmaker untenable.
Kudlow said Huang should voluntarily step aside while Nvidia’s board of directors and federal authorities investigate his relationship with a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence, as well as questions surrounding the possible smuggling of advanced American semiconductors to China.
“The very least that should happen is that Mr. Huang should exercise some common sense, and step down from his positions at Nvidia, including chief executive,” Kudlow said during his opening commentary on Kudlow.
Huang acknowledged Sunday that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer. U.S. intelligence officials reportedly believe she was working on behalf of China’s Ministry of State Security.
Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it had launched an independent investigation into reports that its chief executive had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The inquiry will be overseen by independent directors and outside counsel.
The board said it had no reason to believe that national security or Nvidia’s confidential information had been compromised. It also expressed confidence in Huang’s leadership and said he was cooperating with the investigation.
President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI was looking into the matter.
Kudlow also pointed to reports that Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the preparation of a classified intelligence memorandum warning senior administration officials about Huang’s relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative.
The New York Times reported Tuesday that Rubio personally briefed Trump about the intelligence during the president’s trip to China in May.
The controversy has also raised questions about Megaspeed, which has been investigated over suspicions that advanced Nvidia chips were illegally diverted to China. Kudlow cited the chip-smuggling allegations as another reason Huang should relinquish his leadership positions while the investigations proceed.
Beyond the national security questions, Kudlow warned that the scandal threatens to undermine public confidence in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence industry.
“Mr. Huang is going to wind up giving the whole AI revolution a very bad name,” Kudlow said, pointing to growing bipartisan opposition to data centers and public concerns about artificial intelligence.
Kudlow acknowledged that Huang had previously served as an effective advocate for the technology, but said the revelations had changed that assessment.
“Mr. Huang has been a good spokesperson for the AI revolution, but with these honeypot/national security revelations, he no longer is a good spokesperson for the AI revolution,” Kudlow said.
He also warned that incoming Democratic majorities in the House and Senate were likely to subject Huang to aggressive congressional scrutiny.
The controversy has already attracted attention on Capitol Hill. Republican chairmen of three House committees have requested that Huang appear for a closed-door briefing about Nvidia’s security procedures and his interactions with Alice Huang.
Kudlow stressed that Huang’s departure would not threaten the future of artificial intelligence, pointing to technological advances by competitors including Google, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, and Micron.
“The downfall of Mr. Huang, if that happens, is not the end of AI,” Kudlow said.
The former director of the White House National Economic Council emphasized that he was not seeking to prejudge the investigations or determine Huang’s guilt.
“Right now I’m not here to indict Mr. Huang,” Kudlow said. “I will simply suggest that he set an example of integrity, character, and patriotism.”
“Now is the time for him to step down, while all these investigations occur. And ultimately let the chips fall where they may.”

content:
英伟达董事会聘请前检察官调查黄仁勋的中国间谍丑闻
英伟达董事会聘请了一名前联邦检察官来调查首席执行官黄仁勋与一名被指控为中国间谍的女子的婚外情，该公司在发布季度收益报告前一周正试图控制丑闻的影响。
据《华盛顿邮报》报道，董事会聘请了 Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz 律师事务所合伙人 Joon H. Kim 来领导调查。沃切特尔此前曾处理过敏感调查，包括对洛杉矶快船队在保留科怀·伦纳德时规避 NBA 薪资规定的指控进​​行调查。
金担任检察官多年。他于 2000 年至 2006 年和 2013 年至 2018 年在纽约南区美国检察官办公室工作，处理有组织犯罪案件，包括对黑帮彼得·戈蒂的谋杀起诉。 2021 年，在私人执业期间，他成为审查针对前纽约州州长安德鲁·M·科莫（民主党）性骚扰指控的独立调查员之一。
黄在周日发送的一封电子邮件中向员工透露了这件事，就在同一天，他告诉了妻子。布赖特巴特新闻报道了有关詹森事件中的伴侣爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）的更多细节，她被指控为中国间谍：
Alice Huang 是中国官方媒体的前电视记者，在金融行业工作后于 2023 年加入 Megaspeed。当年 3 月至 11 月，新加坡的一份登记表将她列为公司董事。据《华尔街日报》此前报道，她于 2024 年 3 月在加利福尼亚州举行的 Nvidia 活动中首次见到黄仁勋，两人在台北鸡尾酒吧再次见面。 2025 年 5 月，在另一次访问台北期间，黄再次被拍到与她一起参加晚宴，两人亲吻脸颊并触摸手臂。
台北晚宴几周后，黄仁勋和英伟达高级游说者前往华盛顿会见副国务卿克里斯托弗·兰道(Christopher Landau)，认为政府应该批准为中国市场制造的 H20 芯片的出口许可证。几天后，黄与特朗普会面后，政府批准了 H20 的销售，以换取中国销售的 15% 归美国财政部。大约在同一时间，英伟达高管获悉政府对 Megaspeed 的调查。据报道，英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特联系了美国商务部工业与安全局局长杰弗里·凯斯勒。不久之后，司法部控制了 Megaspeed 探测器，削弱了商务部的作用。一些官员担心凯斯勒与英伟达的接触玷污了调查。
黄周一出现在英伟达圣克拉拉总部，像往常一样与高管举行例行早会。据接受 CNBC 采访的知情人士透露，当天晚些时候，在另一场闭门会议上，他直接谈到了此事并向员工道歉。他没有回答任何问题，然后继续今天的工作。周二，他回到办公室参加更多会议，距离英伟达公布季度收益还有一周。
英伟达股东对中国间谍丑闻作出反应，对该公司提起诉讼：
Schall, Brown & Schwartz律师事务所率先就英伟达中国间谍丑闻展开调查。随后罗森律师事务所提起了集体诉讼。
该诉讼声称黄和

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia Board Hires Former Prosecutor to Probe Jensen Huang's China Spy Scandal
Nvidia’s board hired a former federal prosecutor to investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a spy for China, as the company tries to manage the fallout of its scandal a week before its quarterly earnings report.
The Washington Post reports that the board brought in Joon H. Kim, a partner at the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to lead the investigation. Wachtell has handled sensitive inquiries before, including a probe into claims that the Los Angeles Clippers circumvented NBA salary rules in retaining Kawhi Leonard.
Kim spent years as a prosecutor. He worked in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York from 2000 to 2006 and again from 2013 to 2018, handling organized crime cases, including the murder prosecution of mobster Peter Gotti. In 2021, while in private practice, he was one of the independent investigators who examined sexual harassment allegations against former New York Governor Andrew M. Cuomo (D).
Huang disclosed the affair to employees in an email sent Sunday, the same day he told his wife. Breitbart News reported additional details that have come to light about Jensen’s partner in the affair, Alice Huang, who is alleged to be a spy for China:
Alice Huang is a former television reporter for Chinese state media who joined Megaspeed in 2023 after working in the financial sector. A Singapore registration listed her as a company director from March to November that year. She first met Jensen Huang at an Nvidia event in California in March 2024, according to earlier Journal reporting, and the two met again at the Taipei cocktail bar. In May 2025, during another Taipei visit, Huang was photographed with her again at a dinner, the two seen kissing on the cheek and touching arms.
Weeks after the Taipei dinner, Huang and top Nvidia lobbyists traveled to Washington to meet with Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, arguing the government should approve export licenses for the H20 chip, which was built for the Chinese market. A few days later, after Huang met with Trump, the administration approved the H20 sale in exchange for 15 percent of China sales going to the U.S. Treasury. Around the same time, Nvidia executives learned of the government’s investigation into Megaspeed. Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, reportedly reached out to Jeffrey Kessler, head of the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security. Shortly afterward, the Justice Department took control of the Megaspeed probe, reducing the Commerce Department’s role. Some officials worried Kessler’s contact with Nvidia had tainted the investigation.
Huang showed up at Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters Monday and ran his regular morning meeting with top executives as usual. Later that day, in a separate closed-door meeting, he addressed the affair directly and apologized to staff, according to people familiar with the meeting who spoke to CNBC. He took no questions, then moved on to the day’s business. He was back in the office Tuesday for more meetings, one week before Nvidia reports quarterly earnings.
Nvidia shareholders have reacted to the China spy scandal by filing a lawsuit against the company:
The law firm of Schall, Brown & Schwartz was the first to launch an investigation of Nvidia over the Chinese spy scandal. The class-action lawsuit was then filed by the Rosen Law Firm.
The lawsuit claims Huang and Nvidia misled shareholders about the national security concerns the relationship raised, and that the omission artificially propped up Nvidia’s share price. “As a result of Defendants’ wrongful acts and omissions, and the precipitous decline in the market value of the Company’s securities, Plaintiff and other Class members have suffered significant losses and damages,” the complaint states.
The mood inside the company has been mixed. One employee told CNBC the atmosphere was “sad,” while another described the response as “business as usual.”
Read more at the Washington Post here.
Lucas Nolan is a reporter for Breitbart News covering issues of AI, free speech, and online censorship.

Fundraiser by KIMA Network Inc : Flash Flood Rasuwa Children’s Relief Fund
Rasuwa Children’s Relief ensures orphans get housing, food, and education after the floods
KIMA Network Inc is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Kima Network Inc.
KIMA Network is raising funds to support school-age children from Syabru Besi, Setang, Timure, and surrounding communities affected by the flooding.
Because search and rescue efforts are still ongoing, we do not want to make assumptions about any child's family situation. We continue to hope that missing parents and loved ones will be found and reunited with their families.
Our action plan: We collected data from 5 boarding schools in Kathmandu and identified 41 students who are orphaned or have lost a parent, and who have no sponsor or only partial sponsorship. We have decided to sponsor all 41 students for this year and the upcoming so they can stay safe, supported, and in school. The schools are:
• Srongtsen Bhrikuti Boarding High School
• North Valley English Secondary Boarding School
We still have a waiting list of children who need a sponsor. Please reach out to us or support through GoFundMe to help the children of Rasuwa.
We want to be there for them not only in the immediate aftermath, but in the months and years that follow.
For any child who is ultimately left without parental care, surviving the disaster will only be the beginning. They will need stability. They will need an education. They will need a safe place to live. And, most of all, they will need the reassurance that they have not been forgotten.
• Safe housing, food, clothing, and everyday necessities
• School tuition, uniforms, books, and educational expenses
• Longer-term assistance for children left without parents or stable caregivers
Our commitment is not only to help these children through the immediate crisis, but to give them the stability, education, and support they need to move forward.
You do not have to be from Nepal to make a difference. Whether you are able to donate any amount ($) or simply share this fundraiser, every act of support can help us reach a child who may need care for years to come.
Please keep the families of Rasuwa in your thoughts, and if you are able, please stand with the children whose lives may be changed forever by this disaster.

content:
Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family

content:
Fundraiser by Tarra Subhar Massallo : Immediate aid for families affected by the Nepal-Tibet Flood
This fund provides direct aid for shelter, food, and essentials to Nepal-Tibet families
Tarra Subhar Massallo is organizing this fundraiser.
After fleeing from the Chinese annexation of Tibet, many Kyirong Tibetan families crossed into Nepal believing their exile would be temporary. It was not. Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley had become their home instead- a place where hundreds of families had to rebuild from nothing, including my grandparents. Like many Tibetan refugees, they eventually moved on to build new lives in India. However, not everyone left. Some of their family stayed behind in Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley, carrying on the roots left behind by previous generations.
On August 26, 2026, a glacier collapse high in the Langtang Himal sent a wall of water and debris surging down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Bazaar: the towns where that branch of our family stayed and built their lives after losing everything once before. Four households in our family were directly affected:
Our cousin Dawa Dakpa (confirmed deceased) leaves behind a wife and two young children.
Aku Jangchup, his wife, and child (confirmed deceased)
Nama Nangsa Ghongma's family and relatives (missing)
Nama Karmo Subhar's family and relatives (missing)
Now, our families face rebuilding once again, with roads and homes submerged in mud. 100% of every contribution will go directly to these impacted families and the wider flood-affected communities as they recover together. The funds will be spent on various essentials based on each family's needs (including, but not limited to: temporary shelter, food, emergency medical care, and transportation costs). We invite you to help write the next chapter of this story. Please help support this fundraiser in any way that you can.
My name is Tarra Subhar Massallo. I am the granddaughter of Tibetan refugees who fled from Kyirong during the 1959 Chinese annexation of Tibet, and the daughter of a Tibetan immigrant mother who moved from India to the United States with her family in search of a better life. Growing up in a mixed household, I am surrounded by the importance of my many cultures and giving back to my respective communities.

Fundraiser by Dominic Urso : Help Bhujung Rebuild After the Tibet-Nepal Flood
Bhujung’s fund covers urgent food, shelter, and essentials lost in the recent Syabru Besi flood
Dominic Urso is organizing this fundraiser.
Dominic and Kayla are raising funds for Bhujung Tamang, a friend they met while traveling in Nepal before/after the Langtang trek. During that trip, Dominic and Kayla stayed with Bhujung for a few days in his village of Syabru Besi. Bhujung welcomed them with kindness and gave them a truly special local experience they have never forgotten. Now, after a devastating flood destroyed Syabru Besi, Bhujung is facing an unimaginable loss. His home and hotel were destroyed, many of his friends were killed or are missing, and he lost all of his possessions in the disaster. It is estimated that Syabru Besi still has 1300 people missing.
Dominic and Kayla met Bhujung by chance while starting their 7 day hike up the Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's premier hiking destinations. They were looking for a place to stay and found the only hotel in the Old Village of Syabru Besi. Upon getting to know Bhujung, Dominic and Kayla discovered that they were the first guests Bhujung had had in almost 3 years because he was taking care of his late mother's declining health. As a token of gratitude and friendship, Bhujung gifted Dominic and Kayla a hand stitched bag his mother made pictured above.
This fundraiser is meant to provide direct relief to Bhujung as he begins the long process of recovering and rebuilding after this tragedy. The money raised will go directly to him to help support his immediate needs (food, housing, etc.) and give him a foundation to move forward after losing so much. Dominic and Kayla are asking for donations of any amount to help Bhujung through this heartbreaking time. If you are able to give, thank you for showing compassion and support to someone who once showed such generosity to travelers far from home. Please consider donating and sharing this fundraiser to help Bhujung rebuild his life.

Fundraiser by Craig De Meillon : Support Craig’s Mission to Aid Nepal Tibet Mudslide Victims
Craig’s campaign funds deployment, equipment, and communications for mudslide rescue work
Craig De Meillon is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Craig De Meillon, and I am based in Miami, Florida. I work in safety and emergency management and am a trained firefighter and EMT with professional experience responding to disasters, emergencies, and humanitarian situations.
I am raising these funds as an independent volunteer to support my deployment to the areas affected by the recent mudslides and flooding in Nepal near the China border. I am not a family member or representative of anyone affected by the disaster, nor am I collecting these funds on behalf of a government agency or other organization. I am responding independently based on my emergency-response experience and my ability to bring useful communications and search equipment into the field.
The funds raised will be used primarily to cover the direct costs of my deployment and emergency-response work. This includes my airfare and ground transportation to and within the affected region, accommodation and essential field logistics, food and other necessary expenses while deployed, and emergency-response equipment and supplies.
A significant part of the funding will also be used for search and communications capabilities. This may include purchasing or renting drones that can be used to conduct aerial searches, assess inaccessible areas, locate people who may be stranded or missing, and help response teams understand conditions on the ground. Funds will also be used for satellite communications equipment and associated Starlink service costs so that I can maintain reliable communications in areas where local telecommunications infrastructure may be damaged, unavailable, or overloaded.
Where practical, I may purchase essential supplies locally rather than transporting them from the United States. This allows funds to be used more efficiently and can also support local businesses and responders.
The primary beneficiary of this fundraiser is me, Craig De Meillon, because the funds are being raised to cover the actual expenses I incur while independently deploying and carrying out this emergency-response work. The money is not being raised for personal profit or general living expenses. It is intended to offset the costs directly associated with the mission, including travel, equipment, communications, transportation, and necessary field expenses.
Once on the ground, I will coordinate as appropriate with local emergency responders, humanitarian organizations, community leaders, and other response personnel to determine where my skills, equipment, and communications capabilities can be most useful. My role and activities may change depending on the needs identified in the affected areas and the accessibility and safety of the region.
I will keep records of mission-related expenses and provide updates throughout the deployment so donors can understand how the funds are being used and what work is being carried out on the ground.
Thank you to everyone who contributes, shares this fundraiser, or supports the response in any way. Every contribution helps make it possible for me to get the equipment, communications, and resources needed to reach affected areas and assist where I can. Flood

Fundraiser by Kurshat Uyghur : Support Uyghur film & tell the story together
Kurshat Uyghur is organizing this fundraiser.
We've been making preparation for this film for nearly a year. It is a story of a young Uyghur man’s life in exile after losing contact with his family members. We have received funding from a few organizations, but not quite enough for the entire production process. So we decided to ask for help from those of you who care about the Uyghurs and the work that we’re doing. Our goal is to reach $10,000.
If you have any interest in Uyghur culture or the Uyghur film industry, then please consider a contribution. Your small act of kindness will greatly enhance this film, you will not be disappointed. This film will open your eyes to stories from a beautiful and marginalized people group
The film will be released on March 21st, 2023. All donors will be listed in the end credits and receive a steamable/ download link to the film, and donors who give $100 or more contributions will receive special thanks and additional gifts as shown below:
$100 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film and a handwritten thank you letter.
$200 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter.
$500 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter also your name will be present on the director's special thanks section ending of the film.
$5000 donation - you will receive all of the above and will be credited as a co-producer.
Shirzat, an Uyghur international student who has just graduated from college in the United States, had big dreams for his future prior to undertaking his education. He had planned to return to his homeland to take over his father's business, marry his long-term girlfriend, build a happy family, and become a successful entrepreneur. But with the sudden implementation of China's arbitrary mass abduction policy, millions of Uyghurs, like his father, were taken and have disappeared. For Shirzat, who wasn’t able to pursue his studies due to the crisis back home, this was tragic. He felt he had been thrown from the sky to the ground. With finances in ruins, his father missing, his family in danger, his relationship hanging by a thread, he soon spiraled into a cloud of depression and compulsive attention to politics. He withdrew from his relationships with his friends and put his life on hold while struggling to overcome his painful reality and searching for hope in the midst of it.
We will work with some of the most talented people around the world. The Director and screenwriter of this film have decades of experience in the industry. He has also made a number of short films while in university, many of which won the best picture of the year at regional and international film festivals. Our core team members are creative-minded people who have participated in numerous film projects. We have absolute confidence that we will work together as one and give the audiences astonishing results.

summary: Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser. The Contemporary Uyghur An
content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Nurnisa Kurban is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Uyghur Academic Foundation.
Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

content:
Fundraiser for Silkroad Uyghur by Sarah Elder : Help our local Uyghur restaurant!
Sarah Elder is organizing this fundraiser on behalf of Silkroad Uyghur.
In 2018, Gairatjan Rozi, a talented Uyghur chef, trained in Europe and now settled in America, opened 'Marco & Polo' in Hyattsville. The restaurant's menu features the cuisine of his homeland, in the Uyghur Autonomous Region of China, with classic Uyghur dishes including hand-pulled laghman noodles, dumplings, and lamb kebabs, complemented by more familiar Turkish and Mediterranean fare.
Within just a few years, Mr. Rozi and his restaurant has earned the love of our community. His food & restaurant has been featured in the local press and has earned a dedicated following in the Washington DC region.
Unfortunately the COVID-19 pandemic is forcing Mr. Rozi to close his family-run kitchen, shutter his beloved restaurant, and put in storage his colorful collection of Uyghur artifacts which decorate 'Marco & Polo.'
But Mr. Rozi is hopeful. Having dedicated his new life in America to 'Marco & Polo,' he dreams of reopening his restaurant soon - in a new location that will attract even more customers who want to enjoy & explore both the cuisine and the Uyghur culture of Central Asia.
Your generous donation to this GoFundMe effort will help Mr. Rozi begin to recover finically from the COVID-19 disaster and allow him to pursue his dream of creating another unique Uyghur dining experience for our community! Rehmet! (Uyghur for 'thank you')

Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。
